articles_hidden.abstract: The cryosphere plays a vital role in regulating planetary dynamics and habitability, yet it remains unclear whether its essential functions remain within a safe operating space (SOS) amid Anthropocene change. Here, we propose a cryosphere SOS and systematically evaluate its contributions to Earth system resilience using the planetary boundaries framework. Multiple lines of evidence indicate an accelerating and partly irreversible loss of cryospheric integrity, driven by amplifying feedbacks. Key cryospheric control variables either have left or are committed to departing from Holocene-like conditions. We conclude that the cryosphere has breached its SOS and is on a trajectory that locks in long-term risks for human societies and ecosystems. Safeguarding planetary resilience therefore requires explicit consideration of cryosphere change and its interactions across the Earth system.

articles_hidden.title: A cellular atlas of the preinvasive breast cancer microenvironment
articles_hidden.authors: Siyuan He, Aatish Thennavan, Runmin Wei, Shanshan Bai, Jianzhuo Li, Chante Bethell, Emi Sei, Mitchell Rao, Tapsi Kumar, Chenling Tang, Ivan Marin, Jessica Montalvan, Chandandeep Nagi, Bora Lim, Savitri Krishnamurthy, Alastair Thompson, Nicholas Navin
articles_hidden.abstract: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is the most common preinvasive breast cancer, however our knowledge of the DCIS tumor microenvironment (TME) remains limited. We constructed a comprehensive atlas of the TME in estrogen-receptor positive DCIS using fresh samples collected from normal breast tissues, DCIS and invasive breast cancers. We analyzed 854,911 cells from 159 patients by single cell RNA sequencing and 39 samples by spatial transcriptomics, which identified 9 cell types and 60 cell states. Our data shows remodeling of fibroblasts, vascular and basal cells that encircle the DCIS regions and immunosuppressive ducts that support the growth of the preinvasive cancer cells. This study delineates early alterations in the DCIS TME, including many changes that persist during invasive progression.

articles_hidden.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Yu Zhang, Hu Nie, Zixuan Dai, Liying Zhao, Yihong Wan, Yi Wang, Yikang Chen, Xinhua Chen, Zhijun Xu, Jixing Zhong, Dechun Cheng, Qiushuang Wu, Cong Ouyang, Peilu Lin, Haijun Deng, Zhen Liu, Guoxin Li, Chengqian Yin, Lei Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)–like immune architectures in mismatch repair–deficient tumors associated with response to anti–programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair–proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T–dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ–dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

articles_hidden.title: Atmospheric O 2 reveals a strengthening ocean carbon sink and a stagnant net land sink since 1990
articles_hidden.authors: Eric J. Morgan, Yuming Jin, Elena Kozlova, Andrew J. Watson, Andrew C. Manning, Sönke Zaehle, Yasunori Tohjima, Xin Lan, Ralph F. Keeling
articles_hidden.abstract: The global ocean and land biosphere absorb roughly half of fossil fuel carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions. The temporal evolution of these sinks remains difficult to quantify owing to data sparsity. Leveraging 30+ years of atmospheric oxygen (O 2 ) and CO 2 observations, we find that the ocean carbon sink increased by 0.63 ± 0.19 petagrams of carbon per year per decade (Pg C year −1 decade −1 ) (a mean of 2.8 ± 0.4 Pg C year −1 ), accounting for 35% of fossil emissions between 1990 and 2019. The net land sink shows no robust trend (with a mean of 1.0 ± 0.5 Pg C year −1 , accounting for 13% of fossil emissions), despite large decadal variability. These results challenge many process-based model simulations of the land and ocean sinks, questioning their ability to accurately predict future climate states.

articles_hidden.title: The genetic landscape of canine tumors: Insights from the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA)
articles_hidden.authors: Eugenio Mazzone, Laura Marconato, Antonella Fanelli, Luciano Cascione, Francesco Bertoni, Caterina Marchiò, Anna Sapino, Luca Aresu
articles_hidden.abstract: The Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (CCGA, https://caninecancergenomeatlas.org/ ) is an open, accessible comparative oncology resource that harmonizes whole-exome data across 10 canine tumor histotypes. It aggregates 667 tumor-normal pairs with curated single-nucleotide variants, insertions and deletions, structural variants, and copy number aberrations. Cohort-depth stratification distinguished primary, exploratory, and descriptive analyses. Selection analyses identified 39 cancer drivers, including recurrent TP53 , PIK3CA , PTEN , SETD2 , MAP3K14 , and FAT4 alterations; copy number events included MYC amplifications and PTEN deletions. Direct comparison with matched human cancers revealed conserved and species-enriched oncogenic mechanisms, pathways, and therapeutic contexts. The CCGA standardizes alignment, variant calling, and annotation through consensus pipelines and provides downloadable data and interactive analyses. This reusable framework advances precision veterinary oncology and strengthens translational bridges to human cancer, supporting comparative and translational research.

articles_hidden.title: Climate aridity amplifies global riverine nitrate beyond human inputs
articles_hidden.authors: Kayalvizhi Sadayappan, Li Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Nitrate pollution is widely perceived as a signature of human inputs. Here we show, with machine-learning reconstructed global maps, that climate aridity is also a dominant driver, systematically elevating nitrate concentrations across land-use gradients and creating unexpected hotspots beyond major agricultural and urban centers. Across ~2.9 million river segments worldwide, nitrate concentrations exceed ecological and health thresholds across ~33 and 2% of global land area, affecting ~5.6 billion (73%) and 0.5 billion (6%) people, respectively. Ecological threshold exceedance occurs mostly in headwaters, and about half of the health threshold exceedance occurs in middle-income countries and sparsely populated landscapes. These findings cast nitrate pollution as an aridity-amplified risk, suggesting that aridification may increase nitrate exposure even without additional human inputs. They call for regulatory standards that reflect risks across broad concentration ranges.

articles_hidden.title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca 2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes
articles_hidden.authors: Weijie Cai, Yalan Wang, Fangqian Huang, Yulou Zhang, Mingxue Gu, Chuanyan Yang, Ping Li, Wenfeng Jiang, Xiaotong Yang, Xiaodong Xu, Xiangli Li, Demin Ma, Fan Xia, Zijie Xu, Yuxin Liu, Vanity Spruill, Jiangtao Guo, Suhong Xu, Youjun Wang, Yamuna Krishnan, Liping Qiu, Meiqin Hu, Haoxing Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Lysosomal Ca 2+ release from acidic stores is critical for lysosomal function, yet the molecular identity of the Ca 2+ uptake conduit has remained elusive. We used a Ca 2+ -imaging–based genetic screen of the lysosomal membrane proteome to identify TMEM184 family proteins as lysosomal Ca 2+ transporters (LyCaTs) essential for Ca 2+ uptake and refilling. TMEM184 selectively transported Ca 2+ while excluding monovalent cations. Loss of TMEM184B/C depleted lysosomal Ca 2+ stores, diminished Ca 2+ release, and disrupted lysosomal exocytosis, biogenesis, and membrane repair, thus phenocopying the release channel transient receptor potential mucolipin 1 (TRPML1) deficiency. Moreover, a human TMEM184B mutation associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder compromised lysosomal Ca 2+ transport, and Tmem184b -deficient mice exhibited profound motor impairment. Thus, TMEM184 constitutes the long-sought Ca 2+ uptake and refilling mechanism that governs lysosomal signaling and homeostasis.

articles_hidden.title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
articles_hidden.authors: Zachary M. Geballe, Jing Yang, Vasilije V. Dobrosavljevic, Francesca Miozzi, Nathan Sime, Suzy M. Vitale, Peter E. Driscoll, Peter E. van Keken, Ryan Tappero, Wenjun Liu, Stella Chariton, Vitali B. Prakapenka, Yue Meng, Michael J. Walter
articles_hidden.abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth’s core. Here we use a new high-pressure method – microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells – to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 μ Ω cm measurement of liquid iron’s resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today’s lowermost mantle is fully solid.

articles_hidden.title: Limited genomic predictability of complex trait evolution despite genotype-phenotype stability
articles_hidden.authors: J. A. Smiley-Rhodes, M. C. Bitter, S. Berardi, J. Beltz, D. A. Petrov, P. Schmidt
articles_hidden.abstract: Whether genomic data can be used to effectively predict adaptation in natural populations is unknown. Here, we tested the efficacy of genomic prediction of complex trait evolution by monitoring genome-wide allele frequencies and pigmentation variation in genetically diverse populations of Drosophila melanogaster during evolution in both field mesocosms and a controlled, lab-based setting. At two points during trait evolution, we produced a high-powered, well-resolved genotype-phenotype map that exhibited marked stability across independent populations. Although we were able to use this map to correctly infer the direction of pigmentation evolution in both the lab and field settings, the particular loci responding to selection were largely unpredictable based on the direction of trait evolution itself. Our results hold implications for the promise, and limitations, of genomic prediction.

articles_hidden.title: Geodetic observations in West Antarctica reveal geodynamically consistent 3D mantle viscosity
articles_hidden.authors: Donna L. dePolo, Tao Yuan, Matt A. King, Shijie Zhong
articles_hidden.abstract: The rapid ice loss in West Antarctica since the 1990s has led to substantial ice surface lowering, regional bedrock uplift, and gravity reduction, as measured by geodetic observations. The bedrock (crustal) motions and gravity changes result from glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), a process controlled by Earth’s viscoelastic properties and deglaciation history. In this study, we present GIA models with geodynamically consistent three-dimensional mantle viscoelastic structures and reconstructed ice history for Antarctica from 1900 to 2020, which explain both the observed Global Navigation Satellite System crustal motions and Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment gravity changes in West Antarctica. This study demonstrates that a mantle rheology including a weak asthenosphere and temperature-dependent viscosity is consistent with both mantle convection at million-year timescales and ongoing decadal GIA occurring in West Antarctica.

articles_hidden.title: Carbon dioxide and amorphous water ices in the debris disk around β Pictoris
articles_hidden.authors: S. K. Betti, C. H. Chen, C. Xie, K. Worthen, S. Brittain, J. Najita, I. Rebollido, T. Beck, B. T. Bolin, D. Hines, C. Ingebretsen, C. Lisse, M. D. Perrin, L. Pueyo, I. Wong, C. Stark
articles_hidden.abstract: The star β Pictoris is orbited by a dusty debris disk, within which planet formation is occurring. The outer disk is sufficiently far from the star that volatile molecules are expected to freeze into solid ices. We observed the β Pictoris disk in the near-infrared using the James Webb Space Telescope. The spectrum shows features due to amorphous water ice (<7% crystallinity) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) ice in both the 12 CO 2 and 13 CO 2 isotopologues. We infer that the CO 2 ice is intimately mixed with the water ice at a ratio of 1:10. This implies that the ices formed in cold conditions, likely in the interstellar medium. Frequent collisions within the debris disk are required to explain the observed uniform distribution of icy dust grains.

articles_hidden.title: ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering drive extracellular vesicle budding from cilia
articles_hidden.authors: Mingli Zhu, Yash Raj, Gary A. Bradshaw, Henry T. Phan, Catalina Kretschmar, Marian Kalocsay, Maxence V. Nachury
articles_hidden.abstract: Cilia-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate cell-cell communication and remove signaling molecules from cilia. The Hedgehog receptor Smoothened (SMO) is selected for packaging into ciliary EVs by ubiquitin chains, but how cargo selection is coupled to EV budding remains unknown. In this work, working in mouse kidney cells, we found that the ubiquitin reader endosomal sorting complex required for transport–0 (ESCRT-0) orchestrates both cargo selection and EV biogenesis. Unlike the conventional ESCRT pathway, SMO secretion did not require the ESCRT-III membrane scission machinery. Instead, ESCRT-0 condensed at the ciliary tip, where it clustered ubiquitinated SMO to drive EV biogenesis. Disrupting ESCRT-0 condensation blocked SMO secretion, and combining forced recruitment of ESCRT-0 with optogenetic clustering of SMO was sufficient to reconstitute EV budding. Thus, ESCRT-0 condensation and cargo clustering constitute a minimal module for ESCRT-III–independent reverse-topology budding.

articles_hidden.title: Quantitative measurement of viscosity in two-dimensional electron fluids
articles_hidden.authors: Yihang Zeng, Haoyu Guo, Olivia M. Ghosh, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Leonid S. Levitov, Cory R. Dean
articles_hidden.abstract: Electron hydrodynamics is an emerging framework that describes dynamics of interacting electron systems as conventional fluids. Although evidence for hydrodynamic-like transport has been reported in a variety of two-dimensional materials, precise quantitative measurement of the core parameter, electron viscosity, remains challenging. In this work, we demonstrate that magnetoresistance in Corbino-shaped graphene devices offers a simultaneous ohmmeter and viscosometer capability, allowing us to disentangle the individual ohmic and viscous contributions to transport, even near viscous-ohmic crossover. In both monolayer and bilayer graphene, the effective electron-electron scattering rate scales linearly with temperature, deviating markedly from the T 2 dependence expected in conventional Fermi liquids. Instead, it is consistent with a recently identified tomographic fluid regime, theoretically predicted to be generic for two-dimensional electron systems.

articles_hidden.title: A trapped catalytic product acts as molecular glue for innate immune signalosome assembly
articles_hidden.authors: Qi Liu, Zhongjian Bai, Tianyi Liu, Fangshuai Jia, Yi Ji, Canxi Chen, Yao Gong, Liuyuan Duan, Jiahui Zhou, Qian Guo, Ling Zhu, Huarui Kang, Haiyong Wang, Zhewen Shen, Xiaoxiang Huang, Jiayi Shen, Wenguang Shao, Junbiao Chang, Jijie Chai, Yixiao Zhang, Zhifu Han, Chenlu Zhang, Zehan Hu
articles_hidden.abstract: Innate immune systems of living organisms are essential for host defense. Central to these systems is the Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) domain, an evolutionarily conserved module. From antiphage systems in prokaryotes to innate immune systems in plants, TIR domains have catalytic activity. However, TIR domains within animal innate immune receptors, such as Toll-like receptors (TLRs), have been considered as scaffolds for adaptor recruitment. We report that the TLR4 TIR domain possesses an allosterically activated nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD + ) hydrolase (NADase) activity that operates in a single-turnover manner. Its product, adenosine diphosphate ribose, is not released but entrapped as a “molecular glue,” stabilizing a composite catalytic pocket with adaptor TIR domain–containing adaptor protein (TIRAP) to nucleate signalosome assembly. This “produce-and-trap” mechanism represents a signaling mode that integrates enzymatic activity with adaptor function to drive downstream signaling.

articles_hidden.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants
articles_hidden.authors: Anastasia E. Madsen, T. V. Pushpakumara, U. Sameera Weerathunga, Devaka K. Weerakoon, Shermin de Silva
articles_hidden.abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

Lupini, Miaofang Chi, Juan Carlos Idrobo, Evgeny Y. Tsymbal, Alexei Gruverman, Rohan Mishra, Xiaoshan Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Antiferroelectricity is a material property characterized by alternating electric dipoles spontaneously ordered in antiparallel directions. Antiferroelectrics are promising for energy storage, solid-state cooling, and memory technologies; however, these materials are scarce, and their scalability remains largely unexplored. In this work, we demonstrated that single-crystalline hafnia, a lead-free complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)–compatible material, exhibits antiferroelectricity under compressive-strain conditions. We observed antiparallel sublattice polarization and stable double hysteresis in single-crystalline (111)-oriented epitaxial lanthanum (La)–doped hafnia films grown on yttrium-stabilized zirconia and showed that the antipolar orthorhombic phase of hafnia adheres to the Kittel model of antiferroelectricity. Compressive strain strengthens the orthorhombic order in thinner La-doped hafnia films, achieving a very high ordering temperature of 850°C in the two-dimensional limit, highlighting hafnia’s potential for advanced antiferroelectric devices.

articles.title: Does government-assisted relocation help households
articles.abstract: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency’s property acquisition (“buyout”) program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. By comparing households facing similar mapped flood risks, I estimate the program’s effects on relocation, residence in high-risk flood areas, and financial outcomes. Households that participate are more likely to relocate outside Federal Emergency Management Agency–designated flood hazard areas and experience short-term reductions in debt and improvements in neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. However, these benefits are concentrated among participants from wealthier and predominantly white neighborhoods, who relocate more quickly and achieve larger reductions in risk. A benefit-cost analysis shows that the program value depends on implementation costs and realized reductions in flood-risk exposure, with benefit-cost ratios ranging from 0.84 to 1.28 across three scenarios. These results show that government-assisted relocation can be an effective adaptation tool, but its social and economic benefits remain unevenly distributed.

articles.title: The persistent multidomain health effects of the early-life exposome
articles.authors: Augusto Anguita Ruiz, Ines Amine, Chongliang Luo, Alicia Guillien, María Arteaga, Adrià Setó-Llorens, Nikos Stratakis, Lea Maitre, Nuria Güil-Oumrait, Marina Ruiz-Rivera, Parisa Montazeri, Jose Urquiza, Mark Nieuwenhuijsen, Cathrine Thomsen, Line Småstuen Haug, Berit Granum, Sandra Andrusaityte, Regina Grazuleviciene, Audrius Dedele, Wenlun Yuan, Barbara Heude, Rosemary McEachan, Marina Vafeiadi, Leda Chatzi, John Wright, Tiffany C. Yang, Claire Philippat, Juan R. Gonzalez, Rémy Slama, Martine Vrijheid, Xavier Basagaña, Valérie Siroux
articles.abstract: The environments experienced early in life can shape health across multiple body systems, yet most research on exposome health effects has focused on isolated exposure windows and health outcomes, limiting understanding of their combined and enduring effects. Leveraging the Human Early Life Exposome (HELIX) European cohort—the largest exposome dataset from the general pediatric population—we studied 586 mother-child pairs with nearly 200 prenatal and childhood exposures, including air pollutants, chemicals, lifestyle (diet, physical activity, and toxic habits), and neighborhood outdoors factors. Associations between these exposures and 11 outcomes across mental health, cardiometabolic, respiratory, and allergic domains, assessed in both childhood (6 to 11 years) and adolescence (12 to 18 years) were sought using an outcome-wide exposure-wide analysis. We identified a set of “master regulator” exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence. By providing an atlas of exposome-health associations across developmental stages—available as an open-access interactive resource—this work pinpoints critical early-life risks and offers a platform to guide prevention and policy.

articles_hidden.title: Mechanical forces enable human stem cell modeling of protein aggregation cardiomyopathy
articles_hidden.authors: Yasaman Kargar Gaz Kooh, Bahareh Bahmani, Chen Zhao, Ganesh Malayath, Anastasia Khokhlova, Leah Hayem, Hertier Umuragwa, Hanxun Jin, Ghiska Ramahdita, Xiangjun Peng, Huanzhu Jiang, Javier Santiago Perez, Hsin-Yi Cindy Chou, Jonathan R. Silva, Xiucui Ma, Guy M. Genin, David R. Rawnsley, Abhinav Diwan, Nathaniel Huebsch
articles_hidden.abstract: Inherited cardiomyopathies are the leading cause of heart failure in young adults, with limited therapeutic options. Desmin-related cardiomyopathy (DRM), caused by mutations to cytoskeletal proteins and their chaperones, exemplifies this challenge: Here, protein quality control is compromised, leading to toxic protein aggregates that destroy cardiomyocyte contractile machinery. One of the deadliest DRM mutations in the chaperone protein αB crystallin (CRYAB-R120G) lacks a genetically matched preclinical model: Mouse models require massive overexpression of mutant CRYAB, raising questions about physiological relevance. Here, we establish a human model of CRYAB -linked DRM, using induced pluripotent stem cells expressing CRYAB-R120G at near-endogenous levels. We show that three-dimensional mechanical loading, but not fatty acid–based metabolic maturation media, is essential for expressing Desmin, whose aggregation defines DRM. Using microengineered heart tissues, we found that contractile deficits are associated with impaired calcium handling, pointing to electromechanical uncoupling in DRM. Treatment with the Janus kinase 1 inhibitor itacitinib partially rescued contractility, providing a functional validation of this emerging therapeutic strategy.

articles_hidden.title: A fully hydrogel implantable patch for in situ ultrasonic monitoring of gastric leakage
articles_hidden.authors: Ye Tian, Na Li, Zhangqi Pan, Jiaxin Wang, Qiyun Hu, Zheng Dai, Xudong Xu, Yueying Yang, Sendong Zhang, Xinguo Lan, Qianyue Liu, Lejie Qin, Wei Wang, Xurui Liu, Zheng Wang, Hanchuan Tang, Jianfeng Zang
articles_hidden.abstract: Gastric leakage is a common and life-threatening postoperative complication, while delayed detection often leads to severe abdominal organ damage. Current radiological imaging modalities are limited in their ability to provide timely detection of gastric leakage, while the mechanical mismatch and long-term persistence of conventional electronic sensors limit their implantable applications. In this work, we developed a fully hydrogel-based ultrasonic metagel patch (USMP) for direct, real-time monitoring of gastric leakage via ultrasound imaging. The USMP incorporates a tree-ring air cell array, in which densely distributed air cells arranged in concentric rings create a strong back-scattering effect, thereby producing distinctive and stable ultrasound imaging signatures for rapid and sensitive detection. The air cells are encapsulated within biocompatible, hydrolytically degradable pH-responsive hydrogels, forming a fully hydrogel sensing architecture. The potential of the USMP for gastric leakage monitoring up to 7 days postimplantation is validated in the live rabbit model.

articles_hidden.title: ZSCAN4 links a transient reset of repetitive DNA to genome integrity and cellular plasticity
articles_hidden.authors: Valeria Lucci, Elena Amendola, Francesco Albano, Carmen Ruopolo, Giuseppina di Paola, Daniele Bravoco, Claudia Sabato, Giuseppe Cesta, Carlo Calabrese, Geppino Falco, Pellegrino Mazzone
articles_hidden.abstract: ZSCAN4 is transiently expressed in a small subset of embryonic stem cells and early embryos and has traditionally been linked to telomere elongation and genome stability. However, accumulating evidence indicates that ZSCAN4 does not function as a classical stemness factor. ZSCAN4 acts as a temporally restricted regulator of genome plasticity. Recent mechanistic studies indicate that ZSCAN4 preferentially operates at repetitive DNA regions. In particular, at telomeres, it supports maintenance and elongation, whereas, at microsatellite-rich and two-cell (2C)–associated loci, it has been proposed to enable a brief, locally restricted window of chromatin relaxation. This process involves noncanonical mechanisms, such as proteostasis-dependent removal of repressive chromatin complexes, coordinated engagement of genome surveillance pathways, and rapid restoration of chromatin constraint. ZSCAN4 activity is regulated by multilayered regulatory mechanisms acting at the transcriptional, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational levels, ensuring a sharp burst followed by active shutdown. We propose a unifying model in which ZSCAN4 functions as a transient genome reset factor that facilitates cellular plasticity during zygotic genome activation, 2C-like transitions, and cellular reprogramming, while preserving long-term genome integrity. This framework redefines the role of ZSCAN4 beyond stemness maintenance and highlights repetitive DNA as a central regulatory platform during developmental and reprogramming-associated genome transitions.

articles_hidden.title: Boosting stability and charge transfer of conducting polymer poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) through complementary topology
articles_hidden.authors: Yuhao Geng, Bowen Yao, Yuyao Lu, Jingcheng Liu, Zimo Chen, Shangcheng Zou, Zhaoyang Yin, Xuesong Huang, Jianlong Xu, Jiajun Fu
articles_hidden.abstract: Poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO) is a benchmark n-type conjugated polymer known for its record-high electrical conductivity. Nevertheless, its thermal robustness and charge/ion transport characteristics remain insufficient. To address this issue, we report a hierarchical complementary topology strategy via doping PBFDO with choline chloride (ChCl). At the molecular scale, the cations Ch + selectively intercalate along the out-of-plane direction while simultaneously densifying the in-plane π-π stacking, accompanied by partial removal of H + . At the submicrometer scale, this induces distinct phase separation into high- and low-density stacking domains. As a result, the product PBFDO-ChCl exhibited a synergistic performance boost, with a 2.8-fold enhancement in high-temperature resilience, a 1.6-fold increase in sheet conductance, and a 15.9-fold reduction in ion diffusion resistance. Then, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) using PBFDO-ChCl as channel material further confirm these performance enhancements. As a whole, this work closes the performance gap between n-type PBFDO and state-of-the-art p-type conjugated polymers, potentially advancing its applications from energy storage to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing.

articles_hidden.title: Carrier-free Arg-CpG augments antitumor efficacy by triggering specific immune activation
articles_hidden.authors: Huishan Li, Quankun Lin, Yuexia Xie, Xiaozhen He, Shuai Yang, Yan Zhou, Xue Zhao, Xingang Wang, Yongming Han, Fangli Cao, Lu Gan, Sidi Zhang, Peifeng Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: The delivery of nucleic acids using nonviral vectors represents a promising approach for cancer therapy. Nevertheless, nucleic acid–based drugs suffer from poor potency and rapid degradation. Herein, we report a carrier-free nucleic acid delivery system termed Arg-CpG, which is easily constructed through charge-driven assembly of poly( l -arginine) (Arg) and the immune adjuvant unmethylated cytosine-phosphate-guanine oligonucleotide (CpG). This Arg-CpG functions as both a carrier and a therapeutic agent, thereby eliminating the need for a conventional drug delivery vehicle and minimizing potential toxicity. The guanidinium groups of Arg endow Arg-CpG with dual functionalities: enhancing cellular uptake and serving as the nitrogen donor for iNOS-mediated nitric oxide (NO) generation. This NO production further synergizes with CpG to drive macrophage reprogramming toward an antitumor phenotype. Notably, Arg-CpG exhibits cell-type–dependent modulation of autophagy. It disrupts autophagic machinery in 4T1 tumor cells while preserving functional autophagy in RAW264.7 macrophages. This differential activity results in selective killing of tumor cells without compromising the viability or function of normal immune cells. Consequently, Arg-CpG elicits a robust antitumor immune response in vivo. Moreover, the modular design of Arg-CpG enables its straightforward assembly with CpG oligonucleotides and other nucleic acid payloads (e.g., anti-miR oligonucleotides and siRNA), establishing a versatile and promising platform for nucleic acid–based cancer therapy.

articles_hidden.title: Time-evolved hetero-alkali interphases enable long-life sulfide-based anode-free solid-state batteries
articles_hidden.authors: Jiwei Wang, Man Chen, Mengting Ye, Xiaolin Guo, Dehang Li, Hui Wang, Hongli Zhu
articles_hidden.abstract: Sulfide-based anode-free solid-state batteries (AFSSBs) offer high energy density and improved safety, but their practical implementation is hindered by parasitic reactions between freshly plated lithium (Li) and sulfide solid electrolytes. These reactions continuously consume the limited cathode-derived Li inventory, increase interfacial impedance, and promote nonuniform Li plating and stripping. Here, sodium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (NaFSI) is incorporated into Li 5.4 PS 4.4 Cl 1.6 (LPSC) to kinetically program interphase evolution. Heat treatment initially generates a NaF/LiF-rich interphase on the LPSC surface. This fluoride-rich region chemically stabilizes the interface and suppresses direct LPSC reduction. During the early cycles, the outermost region progressively evolves into a LiF/Li 3 N-rich layer, while the NaF-containing phase becomes buried beneath the Li-rich surface region, producing a time-evolved compositional gradient. Although NaF provides effective chemical passivation, its poor Li + conductivity can impede interfacial ion transport. The subsequent formation of Li 3 N-rich domains, which exhibit substantially higher Li + conductivity than NaF, provides more favorable transport pathways, homogenizes interfacial Li + flux, and promotes uniform Li plating and stripping. This time-evolved gradient interphase therefore combines early-stage chemical stabilization and Li conservation with improved long-term ion transport kinetics, suppressing impedance growth, localized inactive Li accumulation, and filamentary shorting. Consequently, the AFSSB using the NaFSI-modified LPSC interlayer retains 77.6% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 0.2 C, whereas the cell with bare LPSC retains only 32.1% after 100 cycles. These findings establish temporally programmed gradient interphases as a general strategy for conserving active Li and stabilizing sulfide-based AFSSBs.

articles_hidden.title: A TROP2-targeting aptamer enables selective drug delivery and potent antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Yuanding Liu, Zhaofeng Luo, Yuan Gao, Tao Pan, Changjie Yang, Zheng Zhang, Die Yu, Yifan He, Daiquan Chen, Sainan Guo, Yingbin Liu, Yang Sun, Weihong Tan
articles_hidden.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains difficult to treat, highlighting the need for strategies that selectively deliver cytotoxic agents to tumor cells. Trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP2) has been proposed as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC, but non-antibody-based delivery formats remain underexplored. Using protein-SELEX, we identified T17, a high-affinity aptamer that specifically binds to TROP2, and conjugated it to monomethyl auristatin E through an MC-Val-Cit-PAB linker to generate the aptamer-drug conjugate T17-M. Preclinical evaluation in cellular and animal models showed that T17-M retained TROP2-dependent binding, underwent clathrin-mediated internalization and lysosomal processing, and suppressed tumor growth in cell-line-derived and patient-derived xenografts. T17-M also reduced liver metastasis and induced calreticulin exposure, ATP release, and HMGB1 secretion, consistent with immunogenic cell death. In immunocompetent models, T17-M promoted dendritic-cell activation and CD8 + T cell infiltration, while its combination with PD-1 blockade further enhanced tumor control and prolonged survival. These findings provide preclinical proof-of-concept for T17-M as an alternative TROP2-targeted drug-delivery strategy for PDAC.

articles_hidden.title: Evolutionarily reinforced GC-rich motif enables non-AUG translation in mammals under eIF1/5MP-mediated fidelity control
articles_hidden.authors: Haruyuki Furukawa, Abhineet Banerjee, Antonin Tidu, Nirmala Bardiya, Susumu Ishiguro, Chingakham Ranjit Singh, Hitomi Yagi, Hiroyuki Hiraishi, Grant Brooke, Antoine Perret, Kinsley Ochsner, Hailey Casey, Grace Sakai, Megan Freeman, Anastasia Meyer, Keat Robinson, William Finnane, Payton Henderson, Takeru Kameda, Yuichi Togashi, Toshinobu Fujiwara, Franck Martin, Hiroaki Kato, Kazuyuki Takai, Katsura Asano
articles_hidden.abstract: Non-AUG translation contributes to proteome diversity, but its regulatory principles remain unclear. Here, we show that a GCC-rich upstream extension, termed the NAT1 motif, acts as a potent enhancer of near-cognate initiation in mammals. Cell-free and reporter assays revealed that eIF1 and 5MP act as conserved inhibitors of non-AUG initiation across mammals and plants, while the NAT1 motif enables enhanced initiation within this fidelity framework. Mutational analysis identified −6 and −7 positions within the GCC repeat as key determinants of motif activity. Genome-wide analyses uncovered evolutionary depletion of NAT1 -type non-AUG codons in human 5′UTRs, suggesting purifying selection against excessive initiation. Nevertheless, more than a hundred retained sites are associated with genes involved in cell proliferation and migration, suggesting that regulated non-AUG initiation may contribute to disease-relevant translational programs. The motif’s enrichment within GCC repeats further suggests a mechanistic link to repeat-associated non-AUG translation.

articles_hidden.title: Origins of low density and low accretion rate in classical T Tauri stars
articles_hidden.authors: Guiyun Liang, Huigang Wei, Dawei Yuan, Jiayong Zhong, Zuolin Ma, Yongli Ping, Lifeng Wang, Jun Xiong, Zhiyong Xie, Xinwen Ma, Wei Cui, Gang Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: High-resolution x-ray spectroscopy of classical T Tauri stars (CTTs) reveals a soft x-ray excess, low electron density, and accretion rate inferred from helium-like oxygen (O VII). Accretion shock models have been widely studied via numerical simulations and can reproduce observations with appropriate accretion stream structures. Within the standard accretion shock framework, we propose a distinct physical model involving energy exchange between postshock hot plasma and cold infalling material during reverse shock propagation into the accretion stream. Incorporating charge exchange processes, the electron density derived from the O VII triplet shows excellent agreement with helium-like neon diagnostics and standard accretion shock model predictions. The mass accretion rate inferred from O VII emission also becomes consistent with optical results. Complementing our theoretical work, we conducted a laboratory simulation of CTT accretion shocks supported by hydrodynamic similarity principles. Time-integrated x-ray self-emission and temporal optical shadowgraphy reveal the dynamic formation of two dense clumps, the “core” and “shell,” which morphologically resemble hydrodynamic oscillations driven by heating/cooling instabilities in CTT accretion shocks. The core is a standing shock formed by a preheated low-density plasma flow impinging on a carbon-hydrogen foil, while the shell is shocked aluminum plasma (the reverse shock) arising from interactions between accumulated aluminum plasma and its following flow. High-resolution experimental spectra confirm that charge exchange occurs in the shocked x-ray–emitting region. Our results demonstrate that dynamic interactions between postshock and infalling material, mediated by charge exchange cooling, is the reason for the low O VII density problem in CTTs.

articles_hidden.title: Increases in Northern Hemisphere winter circulation waviness over 1989 to 2011 driven by decadal oceanic variability
articles_hidden.authors: Weiming Ma, Hailong Wang, Sandro W. Lubis, Gang Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Large-scale circulation waviness shapes day-to-day weather and extremes. During 1989 to 2011, Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes experienced a pronounced increase in wintertime waviness, coinciding with rapid Arctic warming and more frequent cold-air outbreaks. While Arctic amplification was hypothesized to cause this trend via jet weakening, subsequent studies have failed to support this mechanism, leaving the origin unresolved. Here, using large-ensemble simulations, statistical analyses, and dynamical diagnostics, we demonstrate that variability in sea surface temperature and sea ice accounts for approximately half (48.7 to 63.3%) of the observed increase. A positive phase shift of the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) is the prominent driver, enhancing waviness across northern Eurasia, the northwest Pacific, and the North Atlantic. A concurrent negative Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation shift partially offsets the AMO-driven anomalies in the northwest Pacific. Projections indicate that internal variability will outweigh model differences as the main source of near-term uncertainty. These results refine attribution of recent winter waviness changes and identify an AMO-linked source of predictability for long-term shifts in midlatitude extremes.

articles_hidden.title: All-optical sensing of dermal activity enables an AI-powered wearable ring for continuous stress monitoring
articles_hidden.authors: Md Farhad Hassan, Shounak Das, Dolendra Vikas Addepalli, Leikhang Xiong, Mohammad Shafiqul Islam, A. K. M. Rakib, Samiha Tasnim, Xiao Yu, Emily Rawson, Mohammed Arfan, Antonin Brun, Gale M. Lucas, Burçin Becerik-Gerber, Adam Frank, Yasser Khan
articles_hidden.abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA), a primary stress-sensing signal in today’s wearables, requires skin-electrode contact that drifts and degrades over time, limiting long-term use. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)–powered ring for all-optical sensing of dermal activity (ODA), using light rather than electrodes to track sweat gland activation, thereby enhancing durability and comfort. An optimized dual-wavelength design (960 and 1250 nanometers) captures perspiration dynamics while concurrently recording photoplethysmography. The ODA ring integrates temperature and motion sensors for multimodal monitoring with on-device inference. In correlation studies, ODA and EDA signals showed 86% agreement. In classification tasks, the ODA ring achieved 92.3% binary accuracy versus 77.95% for EDA. In multiclass tasks, ODA outperforms EDA by 100 to 74.58% (short term) and 89.72 to 43.20% (long term). On-device one-dimensional convolutional neural network inference enabled 87.53% autonomous accuracy. This electrode-free modality establishes a scalable, all-optical platform for rings, watches, and patches for accurate, robust, and long-term stress monitoring.

articles_hidden.title: Cocrystals for sequestering and separating large PAHs
articles_hidden.authors: María G. Vasquez-Ríos, Gonzalo Campillo-Alvarado, Changan Li, Karim Nader Samra, Herbert Höpfl, Leonard R. MacGillivray
articles_hidden.abstract: Highly adaptive boroxine organic assemblies (BOAs) derived from a boronic acid and a linear alkene function as a first-generation constitutional dynamic library (CDL) to sequester and separate large polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in form of cocrystals. Configurational and conformational isomerism of the organoboroxines in host-guest assemblies is induced by electronic properties, shape and size of the PAHs through a “shrink-wrap” process/mechanism, which reveals a templating role of the PAH during the CDL assembly. The CDL was applied to separate up to three different PAHs. The cocrystals exhibit tunable electronic properties. The CDL afforded a cocrystal wherein alkenes of two different BOAs undergo [2 + 2] photocycloaddition in the same solid.

articles_hidden.title: Integrating biomass production platform and identification approach for stereochemical assignment of super-carbon-chain compounds
articles_hidden.authors: Fen Liu, Ge Xu, Hong-Yu Chen, Ding-Ming Li, Xin-Yu Xiao, Attila Mándi, Jun Wu, Ke-Wu Zeng, Tibor Kurtán, Li Shen
articles_hidden.abstract: Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C 76 -linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from Amphidinium sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.

articles_hidden.title: The role of network connectivity and transcriptomic vulnerability in shaping gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis
articles_hidden.authors: Mar Barrantes-Cepas, Mario Tranfa, David R. van Nederpelt, Ismail Koubiyr, Luigi Lorenzini, Birgit Helmlinger, Stefan Ropele, Daniela Pinter, Christian Enzinger, Tomas Uher, Manuela Vaneckova, Joep Killestein, Eva M. M. Strijbis, Martijn D. Steenwijk, Hugo Vrenken, Frederik Barkhof, Menno M. Schoonheim, Giuseppe Pontillo
articles_hidden.abstract: Clinical progression is strongly linked to gray matter atrophy in multiple sclerosis (MS), detectable early on MRI and progressing nonrandomly across the brain. However, the mechanisms driving its spatiotemporal progression and individual variability remain unclear. Using MRIs from 2187 participants, alongside normative data, we systematically investigated network-based mechanisms underlying MS-related atrophy. Regional atrophy was associated with functional cortical hubness, supporting the nodal stress hypothesis, and was constrained by anatomical and functional connections, consistent with transneuronal degeneration. Lesional disconnection and transcriptomic vulnerability played marginal roles. Patient- and subgroup-level analyses revealed that network-based mechanisms are specifically linked to MS-related neurodegeneration and may operate differently in distinct subtypes or disease phases. Atrophy patterns were anchored to the connectivity profiles of disease epicenters involving the visual, sensorimotor, and temporal cortices, as well as the hippocampi, amygdalae, and thalami. Network-based measures enhanced the explanation of future atrophy progression in people with MS, providing a mechanistic framework to understand neurodegeneration in MS.

articles_hidden.title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
articles_hidden.authors: Li Gong, Aonan Zhang, Madhura Ghosh Dastidar, Alexander Duplinskii, A. I. Lvovsky
articles_hidden.abstract: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.

articles_hidden.title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
articles_hidden.authors: Ruotong Deng, Ke Li, Rui Duan, Xinyue Zhang, Botian Gu, Lanqun Mao, Wei Cao
articles_hidden.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

articles_hidden.title: Input-specific deployment of the active zone scaffold RIM tunes synaptic release probability and plasticity
articles_hidden.authors: Rebecca Stark, Prapti Patel, Wanying Dong, Caleb Dehn, Dion Dickman
articles_hidden.abstract: The multidomain scaffold RIM (Rab3-interacting molecule) is widely viewed as a broadly required organizer of the presynaptic active zone, clustering voltage-gated Ca 2+ (Ca v 2) channels, priming synaptic vesicles, and supporting neurotransmitter release. Whether this reliance is uniform across synapses with distinct release probabilities, however, has been difficult to resolve at convergent inputs. Here, using neurotoxin-based silencing to isolate transmission at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction, we show that the requirement for RIM is highly input-specific: RIM is essential to empower transmission at a high–release probability phasic synapse, yet is largely dispensable at a neighboring low–release probability tonic synapse. This specificity extends to plasticity: RIM is required for acute homeostatic potentiation at the phasic input, but not for chronic potentiation at the tonic input. Super-resolution imaging reveals that RIM is positioned closer to Ca v 2 channels at phasic synapses and, during acute plasticity, coordinates their nanoscale reorganization to drive the rapid expansion of the readily releasable pool.

articles_hidden.title: Ketogenic diets induce proinflammatory macrophage accumulation through long-chain saturated fatty acids driving cGAS-STING signaling
articles_hidden.authors: Sung-Jen Wei, Joseph Schell, Maiko Sezaki, Agne Baseviciene, Wei Qian, Wan Hsi Chen, Rolando Trevino, Prethish Sreenivas, Estrella Sandra Chocron, Haiyan Jiang, Felix F. Dong, Jenny Chang, Alia Nazarullah, Gang Huang, Erin Munkácsy, Nobuo Horikoshi, David Gius
articles_hidden.abstract: Ketogenic diets (KDs) have demonstrated both pro- and anti-inflammatory effects; however, the mechanisms underlying divergent outcomes on a KD are unclear. Here, we show that a KD promotes the accumulation of proinflammatory macrophages in multiple mouse tissues, using immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, single-cell immunofluorescence multiplex staining, flow cytometry, and RNA sequencing. In both murine and human macrophage tissue cultures, we demonstrate that long-chain saturated fatty acids (LC-SFAs) promote M1-like polarization, while no effect was observed with medium-chain fatty acids or unsaturated fatty acids. Metabolomics analysis of primary macrophages from mice on a KD revealed enrichment for proinflammatory ceramides and hexosylceramides. Transcriptomics showed multiple up-regulated proinflammatory pathways, including inflammasome activation and cyclic guanosine 5′-monophosphate–adenosine 5′-monophosphate synthase (cGAS)–stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling. Myeloid-lineage specific Sting knockout mice demonstrated that cGAS-STING is required for the observed proinflammatory effects of a KD. These data suggest that elevated LC-SFA on a KD may induce proinflammatory macrophage accumulation in multiple tissues, a finding with potential clinical implications.

articles_hidden.title: NIR-enzymatic dual-engine nanomotors overcome cartilage matrix barriers and reprogram the osteoarthritic microenvironment
articles_hidden.authors: Cong Xu, Yuxin Zhang, Yalin He, Haiying Liang, Hong Wang, Yongxi Long, Jingyue Pan, Yicheng Ye, Yunshi Li, Yuejun Jiang, Weilin Lu, Lihan Shen, Yingfeng Tu, Yingjia Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Restoring immune microenvironment homeostasis is critical for slowing osteoarthritis (OA) progression. However, the dense, avascular cartilage extracellular matrix restricts therapeutic access to deep inflammatory lesion sites. To address this challenge, we developed a self-propelled asymmetric yolk-shell nanomotor (mPDA-C@M), which overcomes this transport barrier through a dual drive strategy. By coupling cerium(IV) oxide–mediated catalytic propulsion with mesoporous polydopamine (mPDA)–enabled thermophoretic motion, the system achieves enhanced active transport, in which near-infrared irradiation reinforces directional movement and drives the nanomotor into deep cartilage. Beyond improved tissue access, mPDA-C@M modulates the osteoarthritic microenvironment by combining reactive oxygen species scavenging with mild photothermal stimulation. This synergistic effect up-regulates HSP70 expression and restores anabolic and catabolic balance through suppression of nuclear factor κB/mitogen-activated protein kinase inflammatory signaling. In rat and rabbit models, this dual strategy reduced cartilage degeneration, promoted matrix synthesis, and improved joint repair. These findings establish active-matrix traversal as a strategy for microenvironment-directed therapy in OA and other diffusion-limited inflammatory tissues.

articles_hidden.title: Asymmetric cell division is predictive of human T cell vaccine responses
articles_hidden.authors: Lin Luo, Ursula K. Dueren, Ana Victoria Lechuga-Vieco, Dimitra Stamkopoulou, Liliana Tchernev, Yavuz F. Yazicioglu, Amir Hossein Kayvanjoo, Teresa Lambe, Anna Katharina Simon, Mariana Borsa
articles_hidden.abstract: Vaccine-induced protection relies on the generation and maintenance of stem-like memory B and T cells, a process sustained by two conserved mechanisms: asymmetric cell division (ACD) and autophagy. In T cells, ACD enables them to produce progeny with the same T cell receptor but with divergent metabolic and functional fates upon antigen encounter through the unequal inheritance of cellular cargoes. Autophagy recycles cellular components, provides metabolic substrates essential for sustaining energy demands, and is relevant for the maintenance of T cell memory. Direct evidence of how these processes synergize and affect human immunity is still lacking. Here, we show that mitotic human CD8 + T cells asymmetrically segregate autophagy-related organelles, including autophagosomes and lysosomes. Furthermore, we show that ACD drives divergent transcriptional and functional fates in daughter cells. Extending these findings to an influenza vaccine trial, we demonstrate that autophagic flux follows the dynamics of clonal expansion and contraction of antigen-specific T cells. Notably, individuals with enhanced ACD capacity, especially with increased LC3B asymmetry, exhibit better vaccine responses, linking early cellular segregation events to long-term immune fitness. Last, transient use of the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibitor rapamycin improved memory survival, which was associated with improved ACD, measured by the asymmetric inheritance of both CD8 and LC3B. Together, these findings highlight that the asymmetric inheritance of the autophagy machinery represents another layer of human adaptive immunity and offers a potential therapeutic target to enhance vaccine outcomes.

articles_hidden.title: Brown carbon in biomass burning aerosol enhances HONO production
articles_hidden.authors: Fengxia Bao, Lucia Iezzi, Wenjie Wang, Arianna Tronconi, Yanfang Chen, Therese S. Carter, Colette L. Heald, Kaspar Rudolf Dällenbach, David M. Bell, Markus Ammann
articles_hidden.abstract: Nitrous acid (HONO) is an important source of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). •OH drives ozone and aerosol formation, affecting air quality, health, and climate. Elevated HONO concentrations have been observed in biomass burning (BB) plumes. However, the mechanism remains unclear, hindering parameterization and quantification of the impacts. Here, we conducted flow tube experiments with BB aerosol samples and proxies to investigate renoxification, a process that converts nitrate into HONO and NO x (NO and NO 2 ). Our results reveal that renoxification in BB aerosol is enhanced by brown carbon (BrC) through electron transfer to nitrate as an alternative to surface-enhanced nitrate photolysis. We develop parameterization to assess the potential global impacts of BrC-enhanced renoxification, which suggests that BrC enhances surface-level HONO production by up to one order of magnitude in BB-affected regions, with surface HONO production exceeding 1 part per trillion per hour in regions with high aerosol nitrate. These impacts are expected to worsen as BB intensifies in a warming climate.

articles_hidden.title: Single-nucleus multiomic profiling uncovers epigenetic dysregulation driving hippocampal vulnerability in Alzheimer’s disease
articles_hidden.authors: Quyuan Tao, Ting Luo, Pan Wang, Maorui Jiang, Zilin Lai, Bufan Jin, Yuyang Liu, Youzhe He, Yanrong Wei, Yue Gao, Langjian Zhu, Heyang Du, Lifang Wang, Yujie Peng, Yong Hou, Shiping Liu, Longqi Liu, Jing Zhang, Lei Han
articles_hidden.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) exhibits region- and cell-type–specific vulnerability, yet the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain poorly defined. We performed integrated single-nucleus RNA-seq and ATAC-seq of human hippocampus to resolve gene regulatory architecture in AD. By linking chromatin accessibility to transcription, we identified more than 1000 disease-associated cis-regulatory interactions, highlighting coordinated epigenomic-transcriptomic remodeling. Excitatory cornu ammonis (EX.CA) neurons exhibited disproportionate regulatory disruption, characterized by increased chromatin accessibility coupled to activation of apoptosis-related gene programs, whereas dentate gyrus (EX.DG) neurons remained comparatively resistant. In glial cells, regulatory network inference revealed activation of transcription factor modules centered on SPI1/KLF4 in microglia and STAT3 in astrocytes, defining epigenetic programs that are highly associated with inflammatory and metabolic state transitions. Comparative evaluation with the prefrontal cortex uncovered conserved inflammatory activation alongside region-specific immune regulatory divergence, indicating spatially distinct microglial responses. Furthermore, cross-species integration demonstrated that a substantial fraction of AD-associated regulatory elements are human-specific, with AD-risk variants enriched in microglial cis-regulatory elements at loci including BIN1 and APOE . Together, these results provide a mechanistic framework linking chromatin remodeling to cell-type–specific dysfunction and reveal human-specific regulatory architecture as a crucial factor to AD vulnerability and translational limitation.

articles_hidden.title: An end-to-end machine-learning system for global eddy-resolving ocean forecast
articles_hidden.authors: Xiang Zhang, Yingzhe Cui, Furong Li, Shenghui Zhou, Guangnan Wu, Zhao Jing, Lixin Wu
articles_hidden.abstract: Machine learning (ML) models, especially those based on deep neural networks, have achieved competitive forecast accuracy and greatly reduced computational burden compared to traditional numerical global ocean forecast systems (GOFSs). However, it remains difficult for these ML models to operate on their own, as they rely on the initial conditions generated by numerical GOFSs. In this study, we present WenHai-E2E, an end-to-end ML GOFS that replaces the entire pipeline of numerical GOFSs at deployment time and makes eddy-resolving global ocean forecast directly from multisource heterogeneous ocean observations, without requiring operational initial conditions from numerical GOFSs. WenHai-E2E outperforms a state-of-the-art numerical GOFS in the forecast accuracy. Our results demonstrate the promise of ML GOFSs to surpass numerical GOFSs and provide insight into the pathway for developing next generation of GOFSs.

articles_hidden.title: Discovery of a likely supermassive neutron star in a remarkably wide binary
articles_hidden.authors: Xinlin Zhao, Song Wang, Guang-Yao Xiao, Meng Sun, Roberto Soria, Kyle Akira Rocha, Seth Goggage, Pengfei Wang, Hongliang Yan, Xuan Mao, Yang Huang, Maosheng Xiang, Shuai Liu, Dan Qiu, Meng Zhang, Xue Li, Fabo Feng, Xihong Luo, Xiaohong Yang, Jifeng Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: Supermassive neutron stars ( M ≳ 2   M ⊙ ) provide stringent constraints on the equation of state of dense matter. We report the discovery of a wide binary system composed of a red giant star and an invisible companion with an orbital period P ≈ 1218 ± 3   days and a comparatively low eccentricity e ≈ 0.09 ± 0.01 (with 1σ uncertainty). By combining radial velocity measurements from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope and the Apache Point Observatory Galactic Evolution Experiment (APOGEE) with astrometric data from Gaia DR2 and DR3 catalogs, we derive a Keplerian orbit with an inclination angle i ≈ 73 ∘ ± 11 ∘ . The unseen companion has a mass in the range of 1.8   to   2.8   M ⊙ (spanning the full spread of all estimates), with a best-fit value of 2.20 − 0.13 + 0.14   M ⊙ . This potentially places the unseen companion within the mass gap between neutron stars and black holes. Spectral disentangling using high-resolution near-infrared APOGEE spectra shows no absorption features from an additional component, suggesting the presence of a compact object: either a supermassive neutron star or a low-mass black hole. The wide, low-eccentricity orbit is difficult to explain through standard binary evolution channels, pointing to the need for improved theoretical models to account for such systems.

articles_hidden.title: Electronic hair: Transforming hair into a scalable bioelectronic interface
articles_hidden.authors: Shweta Shweta, Malamati Giompliaki, Linta Sohail, Rémy Cornuéjols, Preston D. Donaldson, Tobias Abrahamsson, Dina KC, Maria Ntzouni, Sıla Yıldız Cengiz, Sofia Drakopoulou, Mary J. Donahue, Maria Seitanidou, Zifang Zhao, Daniel T. Simon, Magnus Berggren, Sarah Mclntyre, Robrecht Raedt, Xenofon Strakosas, George D. Spyropoulos
articles_hidden.abstract: In electroencephalography, hair remains a major barrier to electrode-skin contact, limiting signal quality. Here, we introduce electronic hair (eHAIR), a strategy that converts hair into a bioelectronic interface using mixed ionic-electronic conductive polymer dyes. Hair, a keratinized filament anchored within the skin, provides a stable and naturally distributed platform for interfacing. Two complementary approaches based on polythiophene derivatives enable rapid, washable functionalization of hair bundles or semipermanent coating of individual strands. The resulting eHAIR forms conformal, low-impedance interfaces that support electrophysiological recordings with increased signal amplitude and spectral power while preserving the underlying neural dynamics without gels or rigid hardware. Beyond passive sensing, eHAIR-based organic electrochemical transistors enable local signal amplification, with gain defined by hair geometry. By repurposing hair as an active bioelectronic interface, eHAIR establishes a wearable and biointegrated platform that can be implemented from individual hairs to larger hair-covered regions.

articles_hidden.title: A LiDAR-based reconstruction reveals increasing Arctic phytoplankton production during low-light winter-shoulder period
articles_hidden.authors: Zhenhua Zhang, Peng Chen, Siqi Zhang, Delu Pan
articles_hidden.abstract: Arctic marine productivity is traditionally considered concentrated in the sunlit season, yet low-light winter-shoulder periods remain poorly constrained because passive ocean color observations require sufficient solar illumination. Here, we use 2.39 million spaceborne LiDAR profiles from CALIOP (2006–2023) to reconstruct Arctic net primary production (NPP) and evaluate how active-sensor observations reduce this seasonal blind spot. The bio-optical retrieval model was trained using MODIS-constrained observations under illuminated conditions; accordingly, low-light estimates represent physically constrained extrapolations beyond the primary MODIS-observable training domain rather than direct NPP measurements. Within this framework, LiDAR increases winter half-year observational coverage from ∼20 to 30% to ∼70 to 75% and reveals widespread low-light winter-shoulder production across marginal seas and seasonal ice-edge regions. Pan-Arctic NPP integrated over this period increased at an estimated rate of 0.75 Tg C year −1 during 2007–2023, whereas the corresponding passive-sensor signal was negligible. Accounting for this component raises annual Arctic NPP estimates by ∼13.3% indicating that passive sensor-based assessments may underrepresent the magnitude and seasonal structure of Arctic productivity. Associations with declining sea ice and surface warming suggest this underrepresented production is consistent with ongoing seasonal reorganization of Arctic carbon fixation. Uncertainties from model parameterization, low-light extrapolation, and limited in situ validation are largest in the lowest-light and highest-latitude regimes. These findings do not imply photosynthesis during absolute polar night, but show that active LiDAR observations with explicit light constraints and transparent extrapolation limits can test how unresolved low-light winter-shoulder production may alter Arctic NPP seasonality under continuing sea-ice loss.

articles_hidden.title: Physics-informed and data-efficient machine learning for storm surge forecasting during typhoons
articles_hidden.authors: Huarong Xie, Changming Dong, Yuli Liu, Xingru Feng, Zhifeng Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: This study addresses the challenge of accurately forecasting storm surges during tropical cyclones, which is crucial in reducing coastal damages. We develop a physics-informed and data-efficient model, a storm surge neural network (SSNN), that embeds shallow water equations into a machine learning (ML) framework with a specifically designed piecewise loss function to effectively incorporate physical constraints. The SSNN is iteratively trained to make rolling forecast and can produce more accurate forecasts than a standard data-driven model even with a smaller size of training data. The improvement in the performance by the SSNN model is evident, particularly in coastal areas with varying strong winds. This is especially true for forecasts beyond 16 hours, where the data-driven model struggles to provide accurate predictions. Combining physics with ML could offer a promising way to improve storm surge forecasting and support coastal hazard preparedness.

articles_hidden.title: Noncanonical enhancers control gene expression and cell fate in human pluripotent stem cells
articles_hidden.authors: Yang Cao, Oleksandr Dovgusha, Ayyub Ebrahimi, Carmela Rieline V. Cruz, Stephen Bevan, Lukas Widmer, Fereshteh Torabi, Julia Kurlovich, Ignacio Rodríguez-Polo, Soumen Khan, Manthan Patel, Oliver T. Shiels, Madapura M. Pradeepa, Sean M. Flynn, Ufuk Günesdogan, Stefan Schoenfelder
articles_hidden.abstract: Enhancers are key gene regulatory elements that ensure the precise spatiotemporal execution of developmental gene expression programs. However, recent findings indicate that current approaches to identify enhancers may not capture the full repertoire of active enhancers in mammalian genomes. Here, we combine massively parallel enhancer assays with chromatin structure and transcriptome profiling to functionally annotate enhancers genome-wide in human induced pluripotent stem cells. We find that a substantial fraction (∼40%) of accessible chromatin regions with enhancer function lack key features associated with active enhancers, including the active enhancer mark histone H3 lysine-27 acetylation and enhancer-associated RNAs. Perturbation of this class of noncanonical enhancers by CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing or deletion results in decreased levels of target gene expression and, in one instance, loss of pluripotent stem cell characteristics. Collectively, our data demonstrate enhancer activity for a class of gene regulatory elements that had, until now, only been associated with a neutral or inactive status, challenging current models of enhancer function.

articles_hidden.title: Direct visualization of light’s polarization and spectrum with a compass-like meta-device
articles_hidden.authors: Yifeng Xiong, Shaochen Fang, Haotian Xu, Tianyue Li, Xiangyu Ma, Hong Zhang, Ye Chen, Jinhui Chen, Yu Lei, C. T. Chan, Fei Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of the spectropolarimetric characteristics of light is increasingly demanded across modern optical technologies. Existing spectral-polarimetric analysis typically relies on a limited number of filters and polarizers, yielding discrete and often disordered outputs that require extensive calibration and computational reconstruction. Here, we present a compass-like meta-device that enables direct visualization of both spectrum and polarization by spatially locating resonant signatures. Through dual-dimensional geometric engineering in polar coordinates—based on collective resonances analogous to quasi-bound states in the continuum with symmetry-broken meta-atom anisotropy—the compass-like meta-device exhibits dihedral group ( D n ) symmetry and radially conformal scaling of unit-cell geometry, mapping polarization and wavelength onto azimuthal and radial spatial positions, respectively. This design enables continuous characterization of linear-polarization orientation with a mean absolute angular error of 6.2°, together with continuous spectral readout over the 1450–1600 nm range at a visually resolvable spectral resolution of ∼6 nm. Our approach functions as an intuitive, single-shot, and robust spectropolarimeter for on-chip multidimensional optical sensing and imaging.

articles_hidden.title: Piezoelectrically actuated magnetic dipole twisting resonators enable miniaturized low-frequency antennas
articles_hidden.authors: Jianglei Chang, Bohan Li, Xiangyu Gao, Kexin Song, Yaojin Wang, Jie Jiao, Davresh Hasanyan, Shujun Zhang, Fei Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Miniaturized low-frequency antennas are essential for underwater, underground, and biomedical communications, yet their performance is constrained by the fundamental size-efficiency trade-off, a long-standing physical bottleneck. Here, we introduce a radiation mechanism that circumvents this constraint by replacing the time-varying currents in conventional antennas with the mechanical twisting oscillation of a magnetic dipole. Using piezoelectrically actuated, biomimetic twisting resonators with ultrahigh mechanical quality factors, we demonstrate that low-frequency antennas operating at 15.4 and 668 hertz can be miniaturized to centimeter- and millimeter-scale, respectively, with radiation efficiencies exceeding those of size-matched loop antennas by factors of 49,000 and 5000, respectively. This electromechanical-magnetic transduction enables underwater cross-medium communication over 115 meters with only milliwatt-level power consumption, using 99.9% less power than loop antennas. It also supports implantable wireless devices that achieve a fourfold increase in communication range at identical power consumption, opening a route to long-range, low-power wireless systems capable of operating in some of the most demanding environments.

articles_hidden.title: Controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D photonic crystals
articles_hidden.authors: Huace Hu, Daqian Li, Hui Gao, Fayu Chen, Mingduo Zhang, Zongjing Li, Aofei Mao, Wei Xiong
articles_hidden.abstract: The fabrication of visible-spectrum three-dimensional (3D) photonic crystals (PhCs) remains highly challenging, because existing manufacturing techniques cannot simultaneously achieve high processing precision and sufficient geometric freedom. Here, we propose a suspended pyrolysis-assisted two-photon polymerization (SP-TPP) printing strategy, achieving the controllable fabrication of visible-spectrum 3D PhCs. The resulting 3D diamond PhCs exhibit a remarkable lattice-period standard deviation of only 5.75 nm, approximately 1/45 of that achieved without suspended pyrolysis. Microscopic reflection spectra confirm these PhCs possess uniform optical responses across all spatial positions. By tuning the lattice period and structural duty cycle, the PhCs operating at diverse wavelengths are systematically realized. Moreover, through the demonstration of PhC prototype structures and in situ arrayed fabrication, the SP-TPP printing strategy paves the way for applications in photonic microcavities, 3D optical waveguides, optical splitters, and integrated micro-optical systems.

articles_hidden.title: The transcription factors OsIDD and OsSHR jointly regulate ground tissue patterning and differentiation in rice roots
articles_hidden.authors: Liyun Peng, Zhufeng Chen, Ziheng Li, Shuling Cao, Jinge Liu, Ruiting Liu, Jinyu Yu, Baolei Zhang, Xiaoyu Liang, Bocheng Gao, Xingxiang Chen, Jixing Xia
articles_hidden.abstract: Rice roots have a distinctive ground tissue architecture with multiple cortical layers and a single endodermal layer concentrically surrounding the stele. This architecture promotes aerenchyma formation and adaptability to waterlogged environments, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain largely unexplored. Here, we identified the INDETERMINATE DOMAIN (IDD) and SHORTROOT (SHR) families as key regulators of ground tissue development in rice. OsIDD2/3/6/8 govern cortical radial symmetry by coordinating cortical organization and auxin distribution independently of OsSHR1/2/3/4/5. Quadruple knockout of OsIDD2/3/6/8 caused cortical asymmetry without affecting apoplastic barrier integrity or mineral uptake but reduced shoot-directed ion transport. OsIDD8 also controls the number of cortical cell layers and endodermal cells, whereas OsSHR1/2/3/4/5 redundantly promote periclinal divisions of the cortical cells, which require OsIDD8 activity. Moreover, OsIDD and OsSHR members coordinate endodermal differentiation by regulating localization of Casparian strip membrane domain protein OsCASP1 and lignin/suberin deposition. These findings establish a genetic framework underlying the spatial organization and functional differentiation of ground tissue in rice roots.

articles_hidden.title: Multimodal switches exploiting electromechanical snap-through for versatile robotic information processing
articles_hidden.authors: Shengjun Fan, Jianglong Guo, Fei Jia, Jian Sun, Yanju Liu, Metin Sitti
articles_hidden.abstract: It is highly desirable to design and engineer lightweight, low-power-consumption, and rapid physical intelligence (PI) structures that couple with multiple robotic functions. Here, we present a multimodal electromechanical switch (mEMS), consisting of a stretchable droplet-amplified electrostatic zipping structure, a convex bump, and a pair of electrical contacts, that can be used to achieve the widely used mechanical momentary, mechanical latching, and electrically actuated switching modes by simply tuning the applied voltage and using the same structure. We theoretically investigate the snap-through behavior of the elastic zipping membrane, which can be used to endow the mEMS with voltage-dependent memory, and the theoretical considerations are experimentally validated. As a result, we can apply the mEMS array for robotic memory, such as information writing and erasing; robotic communication by reprogrammable information encrypting, decrypting, and display; robotic computation by electrically reprogrammable logic gates; and reprogrammable binary information transferring. The mEMS represents a comprehensive PI structure for next-generation autonomous machines that can better adapt in unstructured and complex real-world environments.

articles_hidden.title: The ZmJAZ14–ZmMYC2 module regulates anthesis–silking synchrony in maize
articles_hidden.authors: Xiangyu Lu, Di Lv, Shuai Ma, Yu Yan, Chunhui Li, Jiameng Zhu, Liqing Miao, Suzhen Li, Wenzhu Yang, Xiaojin Zhou, Rumei Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: The evolution of traits can increase yield potential but may create physiological constraints. Jasmonic acid (JA) signaling regulates sex determination in male (tassel) and female (ear) inflorescences in maize. Although the formation of ears laid the foundation for high yields, the asynchronous development of the tassel and the ear prolongs the anthesis-silking interval (ASI), threatening reproductive success and reducing yield. Whether JA signaling coordinates ear and tassel development remains unclear. Here, we show that the core JA signaling module, ZmJAZ14-ZmMYC2a/b, orchestrates the expression of SPL29 for reproductive transition, BA1 for female inflorescence initiation, and EXPA5 for silk elongation. Coordination of these physiological processes underpins synchronous growth of the tassel and ears, whereas disruption of ZmMYC2a/b or accumulation of the repressor ZmJAZ14 prolongs ASI. Our work suggests that the repurposing of JA signaling to coordinate ear and tassel development may represent a lineage-specific evolutionary burden in maize. Deciphering the link between gains and unforeseen costs of evolution could further improve yields.

articles_hidden.title: Molecular thermal vibration assisted 1208-nm excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts
articles_hidden.authors: Lin-Han Jiang, Ran Li, Ying-Ze Li, Dong-Xue Guo, Yun-Rong Li, Junxue Liu, Ling Huang, Dai-Wen Pang
articles_hidden.abstract: The anti-Stokes shift, a critical parameter reflecting the conversion of low-energy photons into high-energy photons, has been constrained by energy losses inherent to multi-step energy transfer processes.
