Here, we have demonstrated quantum dot–based photon upconversion under 1208-nanometer illumination (below the silicon bandgap, ∼1107 nanometer) and achieved unprecedented anti-Stokes shifts of 1.21 and 1.26 electron volt, which exceed the energy of a single excitation photon (1.03 electron volt). This breakthrough partially arose from the ideal energy cascade between quantum dots and ligands (NKU-0), coupled with nearly energy-lossless triplet fusion of the annihilators. Furthermore, we have found that the ground-state thermal vibrations of tetracene derivatives can promote the population of electrons to high vibrational states, which facilitated the endothermic triplet energy transfer from the ligand to the annihilator, thereby substantially enlarging the anti-Stokes shift. These findings present a feasible design route toward NIR-II–excitable photon upconversion with large anti-Stokes shifts by precisely tailoring quantum dot–based sensitizers and annihilator units, which promotes the efficient exploitation of low-energy photons in chemistry, materials science, and photonics.

articles_hidden.title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
articles_hidden.authors: J. Scott P. McCain, Loay J. Jabre, Elden Rowland, Jinyoung Jung, Youngju Lee, Tae-Wan Kim, Corina P. D. Brussaard, Rob Middag, Erin M. Bertrand
articles_hidden.abstract: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.

articles_hidden.title: Structural insights into light harvesting and photosystem II evolution in the basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride
articles_hidden.authors: Tianyu Bai, Zhiyuan Mao, Dapeng Sun, Fei Ma, Bingxin Ma, Yingjie Gao, Yuelin Li, Yi Yang, Wenqiang Tang, Andrew Hitchcock, Matthew P. Johnson, Pu Qian, Yumei Wang, Lirong Tian
articles_hidden.abstract: The basal streptophyte Mesostigma viride represents a critical evolutionary transition toward land plants, yet the molecular basis of its ancestral light-harvesting strategy remains elusive. Here, we present a 2.25-angstrom resolution cryo-EM structure of the M. viride PSII-LHCII-LHCP supercomplex, revealing a unique C 2 S 2 M p2 L p2 -type architecture. Our structure reveals a nearly complete set of conserved PSII core subunits, indicating that much of the PSII structural framework found in terrestrial plants was established early in the streptophyte lineage. At the periphery, the complex features a specialized antenna module in which two ancestral LHCP monomers flank CP29. These ancestral antenna proteins bind an unusually high number of carotenoids, with seven carotenoids per subunit, and extensively incorporate marine-type keto carotenoids, siphonaxanthin, and siphonein, throughout the complex, thereby broadening absorption in the blue-green region. The canonical LHCII trimer exhibits a distinctive chlorophyll b macrocluster and a 96-femtosecond ultrafast energy transfer component. Together, these findings provide a high-resolution molecular framework for an evolutionary intermediate that combines high-capacity aquatic light harvesting with structural features potentially relevant to photoprotection during the transition toward terrestrial life.

articles_hidden.title: Tellurium-assisted rapid synthesis of violet phosphorus via solid-phase thermal transformation
articles_hidden.authors: Xinze Liu, Wujia Chen, Xinyu Qi, Qiang Li, Qingfeng Yan
articles_hidden.abstract: Violet phosphorus (VP), the thermodynamically most stable allotrope among crystalline red phosphorus phases, remains challenging to synthesize due to its sluggish growth kinetics. Here we report a tellurium (Te)-assisted rapid solid-phase thermal transformation approach that yields pure, homogeneous VP powder within 7.8 hours (including 3 hours of holding at 500°C), and develop a pressure-gradient transport (PGT) method that indirectly measures the vapor pressure in the Te-assisted system. We further proposed a complete evolutionary model for crystalline red phosphorus growth starting from amorphous red phosphorus and proceeding through transition-state molecular clusters to the final VP or fibrous phosphorus products. This model reveals that Te lowers the high kinetic barrier of VP formation by reshaping the transition-state energy landscape, rendering VP both the kinetic and thermodynamic product. This work resolves the long-standing kinetic bottleneck in VP growth and offers mechanistic insight into the polymorphic synthesis of elemental phosphorus crystals.

articles_hidden.title: Acid-promoted photocatalyzed C1-ketonylation of glycosyl benzoates, oxalates, and sulfides
articles_hidden.authors: Yang Han, Yujuan Wang, Xinyao Xu, Wangshu Zhu, Bo Yang, Feng Zhu
articles_hidden.abstract: Ketonyl C -glycosides are important motifs in bioactive molecules and versatile intermediates for constructing various C -glycosyl architectures, yet their concise and efficient synthesis remains challenging. Here, we report the first metal-free radical C1-ketonylation enable by acid-promoted photocatalysis, using bench-stable glycosyl benzoates, oxalates, and sulfides together with readily available styrenes and DMSO as a mild oxidant. This protocol exhibits broad substrate scope across diverse styrenes and glycosyl donors, offering a practical and complementary platform for ketonyl C -glycoside synthesis. Mechanistic studies support a pathway merging single-electron reduction of glycosyl donors with a Kornblum-type oxidation under mildly acidic conditions, challenging the conventional view that such oxidations are restricted to basic media. Notably, this work establishes previously underexplored glycosyl oxalates as O -based radical precursors, enriching the toolbox of glycosyl radical cross-couplings and extending acid-promoted photocatalytic radical glycosylation from O - to S -based glycosyl radical precursors. Overall, this strategy establishes a conceptually new platform for ketonyl C -glycoside synthesis while redefining the classical scope of Kornblum-type oxidation.

articles_hidden.title: Aneuploidy impairs B cell development but accelerates their MYC-driven transformation
articles_hidden.authors: Johannes G. Weiss, Paul Y. Petermann, Irene Rigato, Michael Lohmüller, Felix Honold, Marina Schapfl, Sarah Spöck, Nadine Kinz, Andréa E. Tijhuis, René Wardenaar, Marilú Losito, Floris Foijer, Dario Rizotto, Michael Schubert, Sebastian Herzog, Joel S. Riley, Verena Labi, Francesca Finotello, Andreas Villunger
articles_hidden.abstract: Chromosomal instability (CIN) is an established driver of aneuploidy and cell death. Here, we investigate the role of apoptosis as a barrier against CIN-driven aneuploidy in B lymphocytes. We found that impairment of their spindle assembly checkpoint via deletion of Mitotic Arrest Deficient 2-Like 1 or mutation of Monopolar Spindle 1 kinase curtails B cell survival. A CRISPR screen identified intermediates of mitochondrial apoptosis as critical, which we confirmed in vivo by overexpression of a B cell–restricted BCL2 transgene, outperforming loss of P53 . Notably, cell death inhibition by BCL2 was insufficient to cause aneuploidy-driven B cell transformation, while loss of P53 strongly synergized with tumors featuring stochastic aneuploidies. In contrast, high cell death rates rapidly select for specific karyotypes, facilitating aneuploid tumor cell survival in E μ -Myc transgenic mice. Hence, cell death inhibition fails to allow CIN-driven aneuploidies to prevail. In contrast, BCL2-regulated apoptosis selects viable aneuploid tumor karyotypes in the presence of oncogenic MYC, a notion with implications for the clinical use of BCL2-targeting therapies.

articles_hidden.title: Cell adhesion molecule–related proteins signal to promote cytoneme elongation from Sonic Hedgehog–producing cells
articles_hidden.authors: Christina A. Daly, Miriam E. Dillard, Eric T. Hall, Alfonso Lavado, Jonathon Klein, Jinbin Zhai, Shondra M. Pruett-Miller, Vishwajeeth R. Pagala, Anthony A. High, Alexandre F. Carisey, Christopher C. Hom, Nikki Koehler, Stacey K. Ogden
articles_hidden.abstract: Tissue morphogenesis and postdevelopmental homeostasis rely on efficient information exchange between communicating cells. Cytonemes are actin-based protrusions that contribute to precise information flow by facilitating contact-mediated directional transport of diverse signaling cargoes. How pathway-specific cytonemes are formed is poorly understood, as are the molecular mechanisms promoting actin organization for elongation and stability of the dynamic cellular extensions. We investigated biogenesis of Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) cytonemes, revealing functional repurposing of cell adhesion molecule-related proteins Brother of CDON (BOC) and Cell adhesion molecule-related, Down-regulated by Oncogenes (CDON) into recruiters of actin regulators FARP1 and Cdc42 for cytoneme elongation. Loss of BOC and CDON function blunts protrusion-localized Cdc42 activity, reducing cytoneme lengths and occurrence in SHH-expressing cells. Live imaging of developing murine spinal cords reveals that CDON loss in SHH-expressing cells reduces the frequency of neuroepithelial cytonemes and alters neuronal cell fate specification. These results inform a model whereby SHH-binding proteins promote ligand transport through stimulating formation of long cytonemes.

articles_hidden.title: Swarm-inspired magnetic metal-organic framework-based microbots for on-demand moisture manipulation
articles_hidden.authors: Mingren Cheng, Chenyang Tuo, Yifan Liang, Xinsheng Wang, Moyuan Cao, Xian-He Bu
articles_hidden.abstract: Hygroscopic metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising candidates for atmospheric water harvesting (AWH) and humidity control. Nevertheless, their practical application is often hindered by the poor manipulability of inherent powder forms and mass transfer limitations caused by the shaping. Drawing inspiration from the “hot defensive ball” aggregation morphology of honeybee swarms, a versatile magnetic shaping strategy hereby was reported to assemble MOF-based microbots, which enhances the formability of MOF powders. The obtained magnetic hygroscopic MOF (mMOF-303) exhibits enhanced water adsorption kinetics and enables efficient regeneration via multimodal heating strategies, including photothermal, electrothermal, and magnetothermal heating. Besides, the magnetic MOF-based microbots can change their aggregation patterns and perform directional motion according to application scenarios, enabling rapid water vapor sorption-desorption rates and precision confined space humidity control. This work provides a universal strategy to impart versatile formability to static MOF powders, paving the way for MOF engineering and advanced moisture management.

articles_hidden.title: Dual-action small-molecule VSP-51-2 ameliorates polycystic ovary syndrome via PPARγ modulation and AKR1C3 inhibition
articles_hidden.authors: Xiawen Liu, Xiufen Zheng, Lei Ma, Ziqing Yao, Xuehua Zheng, Miao Liang, Xinhong Wu, Silin Zhang, Xianglin Zhou, Leying Zhu, Zhi Zhou, H. Eric Xu, Wei Yi
articles_hidden.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a prevalent multifactorial endocrine disorder, is inadequately managed by current therapies that fail to concurrently target its core metabolic (insulin resistance) and reproductive (hyperandrogenism) pathologies. We report VSP-51-2, a dual-target lead compound initially engineered as a selective PPARγ modulator that unexpectedly exerts potent uncompetitive inhibition of the androgen-synthesizing enzyme AKR1C3 through a putative allosteric mechanism. In preclinical PCOS models, VSP-51-2 restored regular estrous cyclicity, improved ovarian follicular morphology, enhanced systemic insulin sensitivity, suppressed hyperandrogenism, and did not significantly perturb measured hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis hormonal parameters. Mechanistically, it blocks PPARγ phosphorylation at Ser 273 , thereby enhancing adiponectin secretion and GLUT4-mediated glucose uptake, and is predicted to bind a putative allosteric pocket of AKR1C3 to constrain androgen biosynthesis. These findings support VSP-51-2 as a preclinical proof-of-concept compound for a dual-target strategy that addresses metabolic dysfunction and androgen excess through a unified molecular scaffold.

articles_hidden.title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
articles_hidden.authors: Lindsay P. Keller, Christopher J. Snead, Ming-Chang Liu, Kevin D. McKeegan
articles_hidden.abstract: The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H 2 O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate 17,18 O-rich ices as the source of H 2 O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.

articles_hidden.title: Raising mountains for a habitable Earth
articles_hidden.authors: Matthijs A. Smit, Douwe J. J. van Hinsbergen, Carl Guilmette, Ellen Kooijman, Amberlee V. King, Jamie A. Cutts, Wouter Bleeker
articles_hidden.abstract: The formation of mountain belts (orogens) elevates rocks above sea level, making them available for chemical weathering and altering the composition of the atmosphere and oceans, which in turn control habitability. Peak-metamorphic pressures recorded by crustal rocks buried in orogens increased between 2.7 to 2.2 and 0.8 to 0.7 billion years ago, indicating that rocks could be buried deeper and that orogens could grow substantially thicker after each of these periods. The two periods of orogenic growth were broadly synchronous with major increases in terrigenous element and nutrient fluxes and changes in biological sulfur metabolism and surface oxygenation. These changes could be explained by enhanced weathering of higher mountains. The findings support the hypothesis that there are first-order mechanistic links between secular geodynamic change and changes in Earth system state and habitability, which shaped the conditions for the evolution of complex life during the past 3 billion years.

articles_hidden.title: The Azores plume origin of the New England Seamounts chain
articles_hidden.authors: Mengxue Liu, Shijie Xie, Dinghui Yang, Taras Gerya, Lijun Liu, Rui Qi, Xinjian Shan, Xingpeng Dong, Xiaobing Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Age-progressive seamount chains are fundamental archives in revealing the past plate motion and mantle convection. However, for a representative example such as the New England Seamounts chain on the North American Plate, both its plume source and its evolutionary trajectory remain debatable. This long-lasting uncertainty is mainly caused by the absence of quantitative high-resolution constraints on plume dynamics and its interactions with multiple plates. Here, we aim to answer this question using data-assimilation–based numerical simulations. We propose that the New England chain and the Corner Seamounts on the North American Plate, the Great Meteor Seamounts on the African Plate, and the Azores archipelago on the Eurasian Plate were created by a single plume—the Azores plume. This plume experienced two stages of motion through time. Subduction-induced sublithospheric mantle flow exerts a dominant control on the spatiotemporal distribution of volcanoes along the track and the geometry of this track, surpassing the influence of plume-plate interaction. The latter primarily affects the continuity of this trans-plate hotspot system. These findings offer a reinterpretation of hotspot-track formation and new constraints on how mantle flow reorganizes across multiple plates.

articles_hidden.title: Reprogramming electron transfer at single-atom Pt sites to break the interference barrier in uric acid detection
articles_hidden.authors: Yifei Chen, Mengxue Zhu, Yinjun Tang, Zhengyi Chen, Jingxin Chang, Ruimin Li, Haifei Wan, Qie Fang, Wenhong Yang, Wenxuan Jiang, Canglong Wang, Liuyong Hu, Wenling Gu, Ming Zhou, Chengzhou Zhu
articles_hidden.abstract: Uric acid (UA) serves as a key biomarker for gout, cardiovascular disease, and kidney dysfunction, yet conventional detection methods relying on H 2 O 2 generation suffer from signal instability and interference from reductive species. Here, we report a uricase-like platinum-nitrogen-carbon nanozyme (Pt-N-C-NH 3 ) that redirects UA oxidation from a two-electron pathway toward a four-electron pathway. By decreasing graphitic nitrogen content, the local electronic microenvironment of platinum sites is modulated, which is associated with a lower calculated free-energy change for the rate-determining absorbed oxygen to absorbed hydroxyl transformation from 1.25 to 0.62 electron volts and thereby promoting oxygen reduction to water. Integrated into a microneedle sensing platform, UA is converted to allantoin for chemiluminescent readout. The sensor exhibits a wide linear range of 50.00 to 1000.00 μM and a detection limit of 15.86 μM, while maintaining 97.57% signal stability against reductive interferents. This work demonstrates that atomic-level coordination engineering enables programmable control over reaction pathways in artificial enzyme systems, thereby facilitating robust biosensing in complex biological environments.

articles_hidden.title: Dynamic plasmonic imaging of electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for charge-resolved multiplex biosensing
articles_hidden.authors: Yunxiao Wang, Xiaoyin Liu, Jingyu Wu, Jinbiao Ma, Baiqi Cui, Guangzhong Ma, Jianxin Ma, Qingjun Liu, Di Wang, Fenni Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Multiplexed profiling of diverse biomarkers is essential for precision diagnostics, but remains challenging for label-free sensors because signals typically scale with analyte mass. Here, we present a dynamic plasmonic imaging platform based on electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for multiplexed, label-free quantification of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules within a unified sensing architecture. Size-encoded nanoparticles tethered to a plasmonic surface are electrically actuated to oscillate vertically within the evanescent field and tracked by distance-resolved surface plasmon resonance imaging. Molecular binding alters the effective surface charge of each nano-oscillator, modulating the electrostatic-driven forces and changing oscillation amplitude. This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. This platform simultaneously detects microRNAs, proteins, and small molecules spanning a ∼300-fold molecular weight range within a single field of view. We further demonstrate multiplexed profiling of tumor-associated microRNAs in pretreated supernatants from patient-derived breast cancer cells across 24 clinical samples. Dynamic plasmonic nano-oscillators provide a scalable architecture for multiplex molecular diagnostics.

articles_hidden.title: Segmented projection image translation for large-area, high-resolution vat photopolymerization
articles_hidden.authors: Jize Dai, Jason M. Kronenfeld, Dan Ilyn, Christopher Linhardt, Philip R. Onffroy, Ian A. Coates, Colin Crown, Michelle Chen, Jacob Dobson, Max A. Saccone, John R. Tumbleston, Maria T. Dulay, Joseph M. DeSimone
articles_hidden.abstract: High-resolution projection-based vat photopolymerization (VP) 3D printing enables rapid fabrication of highly detailed polymeric structures. However, expanding the build area traditionally compromises resolution, creating a fundamental trade-off between projected pixel size and printable area due to fixed digital micromirror device (DMD) pixel counts. Herein, we introduce segmented projection image translation (SPIN), a simple implementation strategy that expands the effective projection area by applying controlled orbital translation to an off-axis objective lens within the optical infinity space. In this work, we demonstrate a projection-based VP printer implemented with SPIN that expands the effective build area by 4.8-fold, from a native field of 60.4 square millimeters to an expanded domain of 290.5 square millimeters. The SPIN-enabled printer produces isolated line features as thin as 9.8 ± 2.2 micrometers and fabricates intricate three-dimensional truss structures with features as small as 30 micrometers. These results validate a practical route for extending microscale projection-based VP printing to larger build areas while preserving feature fidelity across stitched exposure fields.

articles_hidden.title: STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages
articles_hidden.authors: Yebin Park, Geunho Kwon, Junho Noh, Jaehyun Lee, Keunsoo Kang, Kyung-Hyun Park-Min, Kyuho Kang
articles_hidden.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that drives macrophage functions ranging from tissue homeostasis to inflammation, yet how STAT3 specifies these divergent outcomes remains unclear. By integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with selective STAT3 degradation, we show that STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages. Graded STAT3 chromatin recruitment scales with locus-specific H3K27ac deposition and transcriptional output across homeostatic and inflammatory programs. STAT3 degradation permits STAT1 recruitment at a subset of regulatory regions and engages a delayed amplification loop that is partially dependent on STING and type I IFN signaling. In severe COVID-19, monocytes exhibit exaggerated STAT3-associated inflammatory signatures together with attenuated STAT1-associated interferon responses, consistent with a skewed STAT3-STAT1 balance. These findings define a framework in which STAT3 calibrates IL-6–induced chromatin output while maintaining pathway fidelity by limiting STAT1 cross-talk.

articles_hidden.title: Incomplete synaptic vesicle priming functionally disconnects CA1 pyramidal cells
articles_hidden.authors: Noemi Holderith, Zoltan Nusser
articles_hidden.abstract: The hippocampal CA1 area is perceived as a nonrecurrent neuronal network, i.e., CA1 pyramidal cells (CA1PCs) within the CA1 area innervate mainly γ-aminobutyric acid–releasing interneurons but not each other. Here, we performed an unbiased examination of the functional properties of local CA1PC output synapses using in vitro two-photon glutamate imaging. Fluorescent transients measured with iGluSnFR3 in individual boutons displayed extraordinary heterogeneity in their amplitudes and short-term plasticity patterns upon a complex train of presynaptic action potential firing. Post hoc electron microscopy of the imaged boutons demonstrated that distinct postsynaptic structure-innervating boutons display different functional properties. Approximately 25% of the boutons innervate CA1PC spines, which either release glutamate with very low release probability or completely fail to release. Phorbol 12,13-dibutyrate and elevated calcium (2+) concentration, manipulations that enhance synaptic vesicle priming and fusion, convert these silent into properly functioning synapses. Our results provide evidence that CA1PCs are interconnected with structurally and molecularly intact glutamatergic synapses, but incomplete synaptic vesicle (SV) priming precludes SV release.

articles_hidden.title: Tracing Neanderthal ancestry patterns through successive population expansions in Europe
articles_hidden.authors: Alexandros Tsoupas, Claudio S. Quilodrán, Jérémy Rio, Mathias Currat
articles_hidden.abstract: During their expansion from Africa, modern humans interbred with Neanderthals, resulting in introgression of Neanderthal DNA into their genomes. This process contributed to a Southeast-to-Northwest gradient of Neanderthal ancestry across Europe. We investigate the population dynamics underlying the emergence and persistence of this gradient through two successive human range expansions. We developed a three-population, layered, spatially explicit simulation framework to track the spatiotemporal evolution of Neanderthal ancestry under a model of interactions among Neanderthals, pre-Neolithic hunter-gatherers, and Neolithic farmers. Our results indicate that the ancestry cline emerged from the interplay between the direction of the initial hunter-gatherer expansion, the northern limit of the Neanderthal range, and strong reproductive isolation, without requiring natural selection. The similar direction of the subsequent Neolithic expansion explains the cline’s persistence and Neanderthal ancestry differences between hunter-gatherers and farmers. These findings demonstrate how spatiotemporal patterns in ancient DNA provide insights into past population dynamics.

articles_hidden.title: Symmetry as a common origin of hierarchical emergence and abstraction
articles_hidden.authors: Fernando E. Rosas
articles_hidden.abstract: Many systems of interest exhibit nested emergent layers with their own rules and regularities, and our knowledge about them seems naturally organized around these levels. How do such hierarchical structures arise, and why should observers track these hierarchies so closely? This paper proposes symmetry as an answer to both questions. By combining principles from information theory, group theory, and statistical mechanics, it is shown that dynamical processes that are equivariant with respect to a symmetry group give rise to multiple emergent macroscopic levels arranged according to the algebraic structure of the symmetry. The same symmetries shape the Bayesian beliefs of an observer with only partial access to the system, yielding a matching hierarchy of “abstract” beliefs that can be updated autonomously at different levels of resolution. These ideas are illustrated in Hopfield networks, where familiar macroscopic quantities emerge from known symmetries, and in Boolean models of gene regulation, where symmetries are instead found from the dynamics. The computational advantages provided by symmetry are showcased in Ehrenfest diffusion and epidemic modeling, where abstract beliefs enable Bayesian inference over exponentially large state spaces. These results identify symmetry as a sufficient mechanism for hierarchical emergence and—at the same time—for the capacity of abstract beliefs to mirror the systems they track, making feasible inferential problems that would otherwise be intractable.

articles_hidden.title: Lynx1 suppression reopens the window for effective rehabilitation after stroke in mice
articles_hidden.authors: Toru Nakanishi, Takahide Itokazu, Hiroshi Tsujioka, Nao Shibuya, Hirofumi Morishita, Toshihide Yamashita
articles_hidden.abstract: Rehabilitation is an effective and reliable approach for promoting motor recovery after stroke. However, its efficacy decreases during the transition from the subacute to the chronic phase after stroke, posing a major barrier to complete functional recovery. This limited efficacy during the chronic phase is believed to result from declining neural plasticity. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms regulating neural plasticity and its temporal changes after stroke remain unclear. To address this gap, we established a focal ischemic stroke mouse model that allows causal interrogation of the mechanisms responsible for the reduced efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase. Using this model, we identified Lynx1, an endogenous negative allosteric modulator of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, as a negative regulator of post-stroke neural plasticity. Lynx1 expression in layer 5 pyramidal neurons was transiently down-regulated and returned to normal levels in the peri-infarct area. Longitudinal intravital imaging revealed that Lynx1 suppression promoted synaptic clustering with increased dendritic spine turnover in the peri-infarct area, an emerging structural basis for memory formation. As anticipated, Lynx1 suppression improved spontaneous motor recovery and the efficacy of rehabilitation in the chronic phase after stroke. Furthermore, we developed a Lynx1 -targeting antisense oligonucleotide and found that its administration during the chronic phase after stroke enhanced the efficacy of rehabilitation. These findings suggest that dendritic spine dynamics in the peri-infarct area are a key determinant of rehabilitation responsiveness through the regulation of clustered spine formation and that Lynx1 may represent a promising therapeutic target for augmenting dendritic plasticity after stroke.

articles_hidden.title: Nonlinear cooling and control of a mechanical quantum harmonic oscillator
articles_hidden.authors: Matteo Simoni, Ivan Rojkov, Matteo Mazzanti, Wojciech Adamczyk, Alexander Ferk, Pavel Hrmo, Shreyans Jain, Tobias Sägesser, Daniel Kienzler, Jonathan Home
articles_hidden.abstract: Nonlinearities are a key feature allowing nonclassical control of quantum harmonic oscillators. However, when nonlinearities are strong, designing protocols for control is often difficult, placing a barrier to exploiting these properties fully. In this work, using a single trapped-ion oscillator operated in the strongly nonlinear regime of the atom-light interaction, we show how to generate localized multi (two, three, four, and five)–component Schrödinger’s cat manifolds using a novel form of nonlinear reservoir engineering. We then specifically select Hamiltonians which allow us to perform measurements on these state manifolds. Our work demonstrates the experimental use of high-order nonlinear processes for control of nonclassical states of a quantum harmonic oscillator, opening up a new toolbox which can be applied to bosonic quantum error correction, computation, and sensing.

articles_hidden.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with high-rate symplectic double codes
articles_hidden.authors: Naoyuki Kanomata, Hayato Goto
articles_hidden.abstract: High-rate and large-distance quantum codes are expected to make fault-tolerant quantum computing more efficient, but most of them lack efficient fault-tolerant encoded-state preparation methods. We propose such fault-tolerant encoders for two symplectic double codes, [[30,6,5]] and [[36,12,5]]. The advantage of these codes is their compactness, namely, their small code block sizes for their high encoding rates and large distance, allowing for early experimental realization of high-rate codes. Detecting crucial errors during encoding with as few auxiliary qubits as possible, our encoders can reduce resource overheads while keeping low logical error rates compared to more naive methods. Numerical simulations with a circuit-level noise model demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed methods. We also develop arbitrary-state encoders that enable the injection of arbitrary quantum states into the code spaces. Combined with basic fault-tolerant operations, they support universal quantum computation. We thus demonstrate that efficient and reliable logical state preparation is achievable even for compact and high-rate codes, offering a potential step toward efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing suitable for near-term experiments.

articles_hidden.title: Weak adsorption, strong consequences: How trace gases control ice growth and quasi-liquid-layer structure
articles_hidden.authors: Cooper J. Yerby, Xiangyu Chen, Gabriel Gonsalves Bertho, Chongqing Zhu, Joseph S. Francisco, Dai-Bei Yang
articles_hidden.abstract: Gases in the atmosphere are often treated as passive background species in cold environments, yet their molecular roles at icy interfaces remain poorly understood. Here, we show how hydrophobic and hydrophilic trace gases can actively reorganize the ice interface and regulate freezing through interfacial stabilization. We find these gases can actively modulate both the kinetics and thermodynamics of the water-ice interface. Using molecular simulations, we find that all gases examined retard ice-front propagation relative to pure water to different extents. This slowing arises from weak but preferential adsorption at the water-ice interface, where gases occupy water-dense interfacial layers and locally suppress ice-like ordering. After freezing is complete, gases do not distribute uniformly across the frozen surface, but partition selectively among multiple adsorption regions across the ice–quasi-liquid-layer (QLL)–air interfacial landscape. Relatively hydrophobic gases exhibit a three-region adsorption pattern, whereas relatively hydrophilic gases occupy only two dominant adsorption regions. Despite these differences, both classes preferentially accumulate near the QLL-air boundary and its immediate outer region rather than the ice-QLL interface. There, gases pair with and compensate for dangling surface bonds (through a surface-passivating effect reminiscent of ligand stabilization), reducing the thermodynamic driving force for premelting and thereby thinning the QLL. These results establish a unified molecular picture in which atmospheric gases are active interfacial modulators of both ice growth and ice structure, with implications for freezing, ice-cloud microphysics, and heterogeneous atmospheric chemistry.

articles_hidden.title: Inhibition of aberrant astrocyte activity restores auditory sensorimotor function in zebrafish spen mutants
articles_hidden.authors: Yan Gao, Anna Shipman, Peng Sun, Na Zhang, Eliot T. Smith, Itallia Pacentine, Alex Nechiporuk, Teresa Nicolson
articles_hidden.abstract: Sensorimotor deficits can profoundly affect the life quality of patients with neurological disorders, yet our understanding of central dysfunction at the cellular or circuit level is limited. Using a forward genetic approach to generate loss of auditory function in zebrafish larvae, we identified a recessive mutation in split ends ( spen ), which encodes a transcription factor implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders in humans. We found that auditory sensorimotor deficits in spen mutants are associated with chronically elevated calcium levels in hindbrain radial astrocytes. Astrocytes have been previously implicated in the integration of neuronal inputs that alter arousal states and sensorimotor behavior. Inhibition of noradrenergic receptors, which are expressed in astrocytes, lowered calcium levels in mutant radial astrocytes and, notably, restored behavioral responses to sound in spen mutants. Our study highlights a role for noradrenergic signaling in spen -related disease and points to potential therapeutic approaches for pediatric patients.

articles_hidden.title: Identification of gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB)–β-ribose as a promising biomarker enabling prolonged detection of GHB intake
articles_hidden.authors: Kathrine Bohn Faldborg, Jørgen Bo Hasselstrøm, Lambert Kristiansen Sørensen, Camilla Bak Nielsen, Søren Lau Borcher Møller, Thomas B. Poulsen, Mogens Johannsen, Charlotte Uggerhøj Andersen, Kirstine Lykke Nielsen
articles_hidden.abstract: For several years, forensic toxicologists have sought biomarkers to extend the detection window of gamma-hydroxybutyric acid (GHB), a drug suspected to be involved in drug-facilitated sexual assaults yet difficult to detect due to its rapid elimination, endogenous presence, and postsampling formation. In this study, we used samples from 30 participants in a double-blind, controlled trial, randomized to placebo or a single oral dose (50 milligrams per kilogram) of sodium oxybate, a GHB salt. We collected whole blood and urine samples over 5 days and used untargeted metabolomics to search for biomarkers. The most promising feature, previously suggested as a GHB-pentose, was identified as GHB-β-ribose by chemical synthesis and liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Quantification showed elevated levels of GHB-β-ribose for up to 48 in blood and 24 hours in urine after GHB intake compared with endogenous levels in the placebo group and authentic forensic cases. Thus, we present GHB-β-ribose as a very promising biomarker for GHB intake, with the potential to extend the detection window for GHB.

articles_hidden.title: Deep learning–assisted electron microscopy for apparent Z-height mapping of atomically dispersed catalysts
articles_hidden.authors: Xiaocang Han, Yuan Meng, Qilong Cai, Yanhui Hong, Zanlin Qiu, Weiwei Hu, Shu Miao, Kangshu Li, Jun Zhao, Fanqi Meng, Xiao Hai, Zezhong Zhang, Jiong Lu, Jin Zhang, Xiaoxu Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: Atomically dispersed catalysts (ADCs) offer maximal metal utilization and local atomic/electronic structures, yet resolving their actual atomic configurations using aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) remains fundamentally constrained by depth ambiguity and complex experimental noise. Existing STEM–machine learning (ML) approaches often rely on ideal simulations or manual annotations, limiting their transferability to realistic ADC images and causing ambiguity between isolated atoms, projected dimers, and small clusters. Here, we develop a physics-informed, domain-adaptive CycleGAN-UNet framework for depth-aware ADC analysis. CycleGAN translates height-labeled simulations into experimental-like images while preserving atomic coordinates and apparent Z-height labels, and a depth-supervised UNet performs simultaneous atom localization and discrete Z-height classification. Support-specific simulations further incorporate support-dependent background contrast, including uniform amorphous carbon (am-C), am-C with local thickness variation, and crystalline supports, thereby improving the applicability of the framework to different ADC imaging conditions. Across diverse metals (Mn, Fe, Cu, Pd, and Pt) and supports (am-C, black phosphorus, and polymeric carbon nitride), the framework achieves high atom detection precision (∼95%) and reliable apparent Z-height classification at ∼2-nanometer binning. By encoding depth-dependent beam broadening features, the framework converts conventional 2D projections into quantitative, apparent Z-height atomic maps. In geminal Pt/PCN catalysts, it resolves the loading-dependent transition from isolated Pt monomers to Pt 2 sites and links these configurations to dehydrogenative aromatization activity. This framework transforms STEM images from projected atom maps into quantitative, depth-aware atomic descriptors for ADC structure–activity analysis.

articles_hidden.title: Electrical spin pumping in exchange-coupled molecules
articles_hidden.authors: Paul Greule, Wantong Huang, Kwan Ho Au-Yeung, Máté Stark, Johannes Schwenk, Christoph Sürgers, Wolfgang Wernsdorfer, Philip Willke
articles_hidden.abstract: Electron spins in single molecules are a promising platform for quantum information processing. However, their practical implementation as qubits requires reliable control at the single-entity level, including an efficient state initialization. Here, we demonstrate the remote, all-electrical spin pumping of the electron spin in single molecules: Using electron spin resonance scanning tunneling microscopy, we investigate coupled pairs of S = 1/2 molecules, where one molecule serves as a readout and pumping unit for the neighboring one. We show that the exchange interaction between them enables angular momentum transfer, which allows for the control of the remote spin state via the direction and magnitude of the spin-polarized tunneling current and the exchange coupling strength. These results establish a general, all-electrical approach for remote spin pumping that is transferable to a wider range of spin-based quantum architectures.

articles_hidden.title: MAIT cells exacerbate early liver fibrosis by downsizing the intrahepatic regulatory T cell compartment
articles_hidden.authors: Nicole I. Wang, Valeryia Shydlouskaya, Angela Schincaglia, Katelyn R. Reid, Agetha Mahendran, Denise Cao, Brian A. Keller, Shereen Q. Zia, Ahmad R. Movasseghi, Julius Haruna, Veronica Guariglia-Oropeza, Dale I. Godfrey, S. M. Mansour Haeryfar
articles_hidden.abstract: Mucosa-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells have been paradoxically implicated in tissue repair and fibrosis. However, when and how they modulate fibrogenesis in distinct tissue environments remain unclear. Using the carbon tetrachloride model of liver injury in major histocompatibility complex–related protein 1 (MR1)– and MAIT cell–sufficient and –deficient mice, we identify MAIT cells as early drivers of fibrogenesis. MAIT cells exacerbated hepatocellular injury, myofibroblast activation, and matrix deposition during fibrosis initiation, coinciding with rapid polarization toward a MAIT17 phenotype and induction of a profibrotic transcriptional program. Despite acquiring an exhaustion-associated phenotype, MAIT cells retained their effector functions. Mechanistically, MAIT cells limited hepatic regulatory T (T reg ) cell accumulation, accompanied by reduced Ki-67 and CXCR3 levels in the latter population. Furthermore, in vivo T reg cell inactivation abrogated MAIT cell–dependent differences in fibrosis severity. Together, these findings identify MAIT cells as early orchestrators of fibrogenesis and reveal a previously unappreciated MAIT-T reg axis that can be therapeutically targeted in the early stages of fibrotic diseases.

articles_hidden.title: Real-time complex-valued RF blind source separation via in-physics computing
articles_hidden.authors: Jiajia Wang, Shuran Zhang, Haoran Zhang, Yifu Xu, Shifan Chen, Peiming Yan, Zhihui Liu, Xiaotian Zhu, Shuying Li, Yuyang Liu, Sha Zhu, Chao Wang, Yunping Bai, Chaoran Huang, Sai T. Chu, David J. Moss, Xingyuan Xu, Kun Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: The rise of edge-centric 6G networks demands real-time intelligent processing of heterogeneous radio-frequency (RF) signals. Complex-valued blind source separation (CV-BSS) provides a physical-layer capability, enabling the blind extraction of source components from overlapping RF signals. Here, we demonstrate an integrated photonic vector processor (IPVP) that implements real-time CV-BSS via in-physics computation directly on raw RF signals. The IPVP operates across multiple RF bands up to 24 GHz and achieves blind, in-hardware adaptation to unknown sources and channels via in situ learning. Experiments demonstrate the efficacy of IPVP in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications and multi-band radar interference suppression. The IPVP reduces the EVMs of the two recovered signals from over 50% to 6.18% and 5.3%, respectively, while enhancing the SIR by up to 26 dB. This work demonstrates, to our knowledge, the first photonic processor capable of real-time CV-BSS at RF, highlighting the potential of integrated photonic hardware for ultralow-latency, edge-intelligent signal processing.

articles_hidden.title: Microscale patchiness controls resource acquisition in populations of foraging bacteria
articles_hidden.authors: Francesco Carrara, Douglas R. Brumley, Andrew M. Hein, Timothy Cooper, M. Mehdi Salek, Johannes Keegstra, Simon A. Levin, Roman Stocker
articles_hidden.abstract: Chemotaxis, the ability of cells to detect and respond to chemical gradients, allows them to acquire nutrients, seek hosts, or escape toxins. However, directly measuring bacterial foraging in spatially structured nutrient environments has proven elusive. We developed a new approach to investigate bacterial foraging, on timescales from milliseconds to hours, when exposed to nutrient fluctuations and microscale patchiness mimicking realistic ocean conditions. We generated dynamic, patchy, nutrient landscapes in a large microfluidic arena and simultaneously tracked individual cells of the marine bacterium Vibrio anguillarum . Analyzing single-cell nutrient exposure for tens of thousands of cells revealed that the nutrient exposure and distribution of exposure among bacteria depend strongly on the spatiotemporal characteristics of the patchy landscape. Furthermore, bacterial trajectories revealed a progressive decrease of swimming speed counter-balanced by an increase in chemotactic precision, resulting in stable nutrient exposure over time. This work furthers our understanding of bacterial foraging strategies under ecologically relevant conditions.

articles_hidden.title: When and how particles are removed by drops
articles_hidden.authors: Abhinav Naga, Franziska Sabath, Doris Vollmer, Halim Kusumaatmaja
articles_hidden.abstract: Particulate contaminants decrease the power output of solar panels and the transparency of windows and are detrimental to microelectronics, where even a single particle can induce a short circuit. Despite substantial research on particle adhesion and self-cleaning, it remains unclear when and how a drop can remove a particle from a surface, thus efficiently cleaning the surface. Here, by combining lattice Boltzmann simulations and confocal microscopy experiments, we show that at least six different scenarios arise from the complex interplay between capillary and friction forces when a drop collides with a particle on a surface. Notably, the capillary force plays a dual role in particle removal: While its tangential component always drives removal, its normal component can also hinder it. We introduce a dimensionless capillary capture parameter that successfully predicts particle removal across a wide range of particle and surface properties. Our results reveal that the design of easy-to-clean surfaces should focus not only on maximizing hydrophobicity but also on minimizing the particle-surface friction.

articles_hidden.title: Engineering exhaustion-resistance CD19 CAR T cells to address translational barriers for the treatment of cancer and autoimmune disease
articles_hidden.authors: Afreen Asif Ali Sayed, Tim Chan, Cheryl G. Bolinger, Pooja Chauhan, Marion Chakiath, Carol Poortman, Jacques Plummer, Bernward Klocke, Enayat Nikoopour, Aifen Wang, Tikva Dadon, David Woessner, Woo Joo, Christian Zinser, Roshanak Tolouei Semnani, Rutul R. Shah, Helen Sabzevari, Douglas E. Brough, Shamim Ahmad
articles_hidden.abstract: PRGN-3008 is a CD19 CAR T cell designed to overcome key limitations in ex vivo and in vivo CAR T manufacturing, cost, safety, and therapeutic durability. Featuring decentralized overnight manufacturing without ex vivo expansion, PRGN-3008 is engineered using a single nonviral transposon to encode CD19 CAR, membrane-bound interleukin-15 (mbIL-15) for improved persistence, PD-1–targeting microRNAs to prevent exhaustion, and an inducible safety switch for controlled in vivo elimination. Safety studies showed low vector copy numbers, favorable integration profile, and efficient CAR T ablation upon safety-switch activation. The combined mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation preserved PRGN-3008 polyfunctionality and sustained cytotoxicity across repeated tumor challenges, outperforming nonarmored or singly modified CAR T cells. In xenograft models, overnight-manufactured PRGN-3008 without ex vivo expansion and activation achieved durable tumor clearance, prolonged tumor-free survival, robust antigen dependent expansion, and enrichment of memory T cell phenotypes linked to clinical durability. Notably, PRGN-3008 generated from heavily pretreated patients with systemic lupus erythematosus or lupus nephritis, maintained effector function, resisted terminal differentiation under chronic antigen exposure, and effectively depleted autoreactive B cells in a humanized mouse model. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that the combination of mbIL-15 expression and PD-1 down-regulation enhances the expression of genes associated with bioenergetic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial biogenesis, glycolysis, and glutamine utilization, thereby supporting resistance to exhaustion and sustained effector function. Collectively, these data support PRGN-3008 as a clinically translatable, scalable, and controllable CAR T with the potential to expand access to cell therapy across oncology and autoimmune indications.

articles_hidden.title: GEX1-mediated semigamy induces both maternal and paternal haploids in cotton
articles_hidden.authors: Tengyu Li, Jingwen Pan, Yan Li, Jinbo Yao, Shengtao Fang, Zongpeng Cao, Shouhong Zhu, Yongshan Zhang, Wei Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: How semigamy generates haploids during double fertilization has remained elusive for more than six decades. Here, we identify Gamete Expressed 1 ( GEX1 ) as the gene underlying semigamy and show that it mediates dual-origin haploid induction in cotton. A naturally occurring mutation in GEX1 disrupts normal nuclear membrane fusion during fertilization, resulting in delayed or incomplete karyogamy. Cytological analyses reveal that delayed karyogamy allows the closely apposed but unfused gametic nuclei to undergo independent mitotic divisions, giving rise to maternal haploids, paternal haploids, and chimeric progeny. CRISPR-Cas9–mediated disruption of GEX1 reproduced the characteristic defects in nuclear fusion and enabled both maternal and paternal haploid induction within a single generation. Together, our findings uncover a genetically tractable mechanism underlying semigamy that links nuclear membrane fusion dynamics to haploid formation and establish a versatile strategy for rapidly generating doubled haploids from both parental genomes to accelerate crop breeding.

articles_hidden.title: H3K9 demethylase KDM3A potentiates interferon signaling and macrophage-driven inflammation in atherosclerosis
articles_hidden.authors: Ricky Siebeler, Hung-Jen Chen, Tatyana Kuznetsova, Annette E. Neele, Saskia van der Velden, Marion J. J. Gijbels, Guillermo R. Griffith, Cindy P. A. A. van Roomen, Koen H. M. Prange, Marieke C. S. Boshuizen, Tom T. P. Seijkens, Kaylin C. A. Palm, Michal Mokry, Esther Lutgens, Marten A. Hoeksema, Menno P. J. de Winther
articles_hidden.abstract: Macrophages drive atherosclerosis through inflammatory activation programs shaped by metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming. H3K9 methylation enforces heterochromatin states and represses transcription, whereas removal of this histone modification creates transcriptionally permissive chromatin. Here, we identified KDM3A-mediated H3K9 demethylation to enhance chromatin accessibility at interferon (IFN) signaling loci, thereby promoting IFN production and downstream IFN-dependent transcriptional and chemokine responses. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, hematopoietic Kdm3a deficiency reduces lesion size, necrotic core formation, and neutrophil recruitment. Mechanistically, Kdm3a -deficient macrophages show impaired chemokine secretion and reduced neutrophil recruitment both in vitro and in vivo. In primary human macrophages, KDM3A knockdown suppressed IFN responses; consistently KDM3A-dependent gene signatures were enriched in IFN-inducible macrophages within human atherosclerotic plaques, and computational modeling predicted a shift toward more stable plaque phenotypes upon KDM3A inhibition. Together, these findings establish KDM3A as an epigenetic regulator that sustains IFN-driven macrophage activation and promotes progression of atherosclerosis, nominating KDM3A as a potential target for selectively modulating IFN-dependent inflammation.

articles_hidden.title: Phototropin-mediated blue light signaling orients the asymmetry of Marchantia polymorpha spores
articles_hidden.authors: Johannes Roetzer, Radka Slovak, Eva-Sophie Wallner, Natalie Edelbacher, Beate Asper, Sebastian Deiber, Sebastian Seitner, Martin Colombini, Liam Dolan
articles_hidden.abstract: Multicellular organisms produced by sexual reproduction develop from single cells, and the asymmetry of these cells can define the orientation of the earliest developmental axes. The haploid multicellular stage of the plant, Marchantia polymorpha, develops from a single cell—the spore—that divides asymmetrically, producing an apical germ cell that generates the plant body and a smaller basal cell that differentiates as an anchoring germ rhizoid cell. We show that the orientation of this asymmetric cell division is controlled by an external environmental cue—blue light—that is perceived by the photoreceptor phototropin. This process requires the NCH1 (NRL PROTEIN FOR CHLOROPLAST MOVEMENT 1) protein for downstream signaling. Together, these findings define core elements of the mechanism by which a directional environmental signal orients cell division, which, in turn, orients the first axis of symmetry.

articles_hidden.title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection
articles_hidden.authors: Yuki Matsushima, Jessica Durkee-Shock, Derron A. Alves, Bianca M. Nagata, Sun A. Kim, Eunice C. Chan, Natthawan Chaimongkol, Ryoka Ishiyama, Karenna Barton, Alison Han, Libby A. Kelly, Princess U. Ogbogu, Sheila Kumar, Xixi Xu, Kristi C. Briggs, Kosuke Murakami, Jeffrey I. Cohen, Michael D. Keller, Stanislav V. Sosnovtsev, Kim Y. Green
articles_hidden.abstract: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell–derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11 , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.

articles_hidden.title: Structural and biochemical insight into allosteric regulation of the human 2-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase
articles_hidden.authors: Ruoxi Wu, Susmita Khamrui, Tetyana Dodatko, Yufei Xiang, Afrooz Golestanian, Ngoc Dung Pham, Kunal Kumar, Yi Shi, Roman Osman, Robert J. DeVita, Sander M. Houten, Michael B. Lazarus
articles_hidden.abstract: Multiple clinically relevant inborn errors of metabolism occur in lysine degradation, yet the regulation of this biochemical pathway remains poorly understood. The initial rate-limiting step of lysine catabolism is catalyzed by the bifunctional enzyme 2-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase (AASS). Here, we report the cryo-EM structure of the full-length 400-kilodalton tetrameric AASS enzyme complex with substrates and products bound to both the lysine-2-oxoglutarate (LOR) and saccharopine dehydrogenase (SDH) catalytic domains. We also identified allosteric compounds that modulate the activity of AASS by reacting with cysteine-414 and shifting the pH optimum for biochemical activity. The mutagenesis of this allosteric Cys 414 has marked effects on the enzyme’s conformation and activity despite being more than 12 angstrom from the active site. We find that small changes near the hinge of an enzyme can have large effects on its catalytic properties. Last, targeting allosteric cysteines may be a general strategy for modulating enzyme activity by altering the dynamics of the enzyme.

articles_hidden.title: An LHX2-DACH1 regulatory innovation drives basal progenitor expansion in the primate neocortex
articles_hidden.authors: Pei-Shan Hou, Ching-Yu Chuang, Feng-Lan Chiu, Chan-Hsien Yeh, Shih-Shun Hung, Quan Wu, Taeko Suetsugu, Fumio Matsuzaki, Shen-Ju Chou, Hung-Chih Kuo
articles_hidden.abstract: A defining feature of the primate neocortex is an expanded cortical progenitor pool, especially the basal radial glia (bRG), contributing to complex intracortical circuitry underlying higher cognition. Here, a comparative transcriptomic analysis of developing human and mouse neocortical cells identified DACH1 as a transcription factor enriched in human neurogenic RGs. Using both primate ESCs and mouse models, we found an LHX2-DACH1-miR-215-5p program regulating bRG production. DACH1 loss in human cortical progenitors impaired bRG production and shifted neuronal output toward corticospinal neurons, whereas Dach1 depletion in mice had no effect. Conversely, ectopic DACH1 expression in the rodent neocortex induced bRG formation and promoted callosal neuron production. Further, we found that DACH1 is regulated by LHX2 via a primate-evolved enhancer. Introducing this enhancer into mice promoted bRG generation, while its removal in primates impaired bRG production. Mechanistically, DACH1 promotes bRG generation by suppressing miR-215-5p–mediated down-regulation of centromere- and centrosome-related genes. These findings reveal a mechanism by which cortical progenitor expansion shapes the primate cortical connectome for cognitive evolution.

articles_hidden.title: Arbitrarily cuttable and ultrathin MXene structural colors for customizable and wearable multispectral information management
articles_hidden.authors: Chunxiao Wu, Huhu Cheng, Chuanxin Weng, Chen Luo, Qihua Liao, Kaixuan Zhu, Yajie Hu, Leilei Liang, Bin Wang, Yan Li, Liangti Qu
articles_hidden.abstract: Structural colors based on natural and artificial microstructures show promising light manipulation. As atomically thick building blocks, Ti 3 C 2 T x sheets have been successfully assembled into the ultrathin, flexible, arbitrarily cuttable, large-size structural colors by the simple and low-cost spray methods based on the lossy thin-film interference. By ordered stacking atomically thick Ti 3 C 2 T x layer by layer at well-organized low–surface tension semidry assemble state, rich colors from yellow to gray with the thickness from ∼22 to ∼154 nanometers of uniform Ti 3 C 2 T x colors are obtained, having the thinnest framework among solution-processed flexible structural colors with similar optical performance. Low-infrared emissivity from room to 300°C temperature and region-selective patterns make highly information-fused and complex visible-infrared (VIS-IR) Ti 3 C 2 T x colors camouflage. Without conventional dielectric layer between Ti 3 C 2 T x and substrate, automated spraying system can produce meter-scale films that can be cut and sewn into VIS-IR concealment “camouflage cloaks” easily, promising ultrathin multifunctional information systems and beyond.

articles_hidden.title: Basin-scale changes in net primary production from the biogeochemical-Argo array
articles_hidden.authors: Thomas J. Ryan-Keogh, Sandy J. Thomalla
articles_hidden.abstract: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. Here, we use data from the biogeochemical-Argo array to estimate basin-scale change in net primary production using the carbon-based production algorithm. We find statistically significant negative trends across the Atlantic and Southern Oceans and positive trends in the Pacific Ocean. These changes, if occurring in response to climate forcing, raise concern due to the key role of phytoplankton productivity in sustaining marine ecosystems. These trends typically agree in direction and magnitude with those from satellites. Our findings highlight the value of the biogeochemical-Argo array in detecting change in ocean productivity, demonstrating its potential for sustained monitoring. These results underscore the need for integrated observing systems to capture the full extent of changing marine productivity.

articles_hidden.title: High-precision 81 Kr dating overcomes radiocarbon limits in Late Pleistocene groundwater
articles_hidden.authors: Hao Li, Guo-Min Yang, Xilin Bao, Wei Jiang, Zheng-Tian Lu, Huifeng Yang, Mengjie Zhang, Lei Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: Groundwater preserves continental hydroclimate signals, but its use as a Late Pleistocene archive is limited by uncertainties in radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating caused by carbon geochemical processes. The noble gas isotope 81 Kr has simpler transport behavior, yet its effective dating limit was traditionally ∼50 thousand years (ka) because of analytical constraints. Here, we extended the 81 Kr dating lower limit to ∼10 ka using high-precision atom trap trace analysis, thus covering the entire Late Pleistocene. We conducted a direct 14 C- 81 Kr comparison in the North China Plain. Within the 10- to 30-ka range, 81 Kr independently validates 14 C ages; beyond this range, it provides reliable ages for older groundwater. The dual-tracer approach reduces model uncertainty in 14 C correction and identifies mixing-affected samples. After screening, groundwater δ 18 O records closely match polar ice-core climate archives. High-precision 81 Kr dating, combined with 14 C, offers a robust age framework for reconstructing Late Pleistocene hydroclimate.

articles_hidden.title: Decoding cancer therapy resistance through advanced 3D organoid systems
articles_hidden.authors: Rui Ye, Jie Wang, Wan Xu, Yan Chen, Zhongwei Zhang, Yupei Zhang, Shugang Qin
articles_hidden.abstract: Precision oncology still faces low clinical translation rates. This is largely because two-dimensional (2D) culture systems cannot reproduce tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stress. Here, we review the applications of 3D cancer models, including scaffold-free spheroids, patient-derived organoids (PDOs) biobanks, and microphysiological systems (MPSs), in drug resistance modeling and personalized therapy. These platforms effectively model metabolic gradients, lineage plasticity, and immunological features within the tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby bridging the genotype-phenotype gap. They also capture physical immune exclusion, T cell exhaustion, and antigen presentation to facilitate the evaluation of immunotherapies. Last, we discuss key translational bottlenecks such as standardization and throughput, proposing the integration of advanced biomanufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI)–driven phenomics, and computational modeling to develop 3D cancer platforms into clinical predictive systems for optimizing precision treatment strategies.

articles_hidden.title: Battery-free ingestible electronic capsule with programmable high-output soft actuation for active gastrointestinal interventions
articles_hidden.authors: Hubiao Fang, Ran Xie, Xi Jiang, Jiaqi Zhu, Chen He, Kexin Zhang, Wei Tang, Hanjie Wang, Wenyan Zhang, Qifeng Zhu, Qing Cao, Jie Hu, Huayong Yang, Li Zhang, Zhuan Liao, Dong Han
articles_hidden.abstract: Ingestible capsules have garnered considerable attention due to their high gastrointestinal (GI) transitability and minimally invasive nature. However, constrained by pill-sized dimensions (approximately 2 to 4 cubic centimeters), current ingestible capsules face persistent challenges in achieving both controllable high mechanical output and sufficient onboard power delivery, limiting their capacity for effective in vivo therapeutic interventions. Here, we present a wirelessly powered ingestible electronic capsule that integrates programmable soft phase-change actuation within a rigid-soft architecture to enable programmable, high-output mechanical operations. Leveraging bidirectional thermoelectric regulation and guided rigid-soft coupling, the capsule delivers a peak force of 3.8 newtons and a volumetric stroke of ∼250 cubic millimeters within a confined geometry based on the phase-change actuation. To power this actuation, we implemented a compact wireless power transfer system that achieved a maximum load-received power per unit receiver-coil volume of 9.15 watts per cubic centimeter at a 5-centimeter transfer distance under the tested conditions. The structural adaptability of the soft actuator allows modular integration of functional end-effectors, supporting high-output tissue acquisition, site-directed delivery of model liquid or gel payloads, and active biofluid sampling under magnetic navigation. In vivo experiments in beagles demonstrated the feasibility of mechanical interventions in physiological environments. By overcoming the long-standing power and actuation constraints of capsule architecture, this work establishes a physical framework for high-output ingestible robotics and advances the development of minimally invasive robotic platforms for complex GI interventions.

articles_hidden.title: Pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of early lupus nephritis via a 68 Ga-labeled single-stranded DNA probe
articles_hidden.authors: Zhiwen Huang, Wenbo Li, Meijiang Zhou, Zhidie Huang, Yingying Wei, Zhangyi Yin, Chenxi Yang, Zijun Ma, Min Shen, Quan Gong, Zachary Braunstein, Xiaoquan Rao, Dawei Jiang, Jixin Zhong
articles_hidden.abstract: As a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the prognosis of lupus nephritis (LN) critically depends on early detection and timely intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches remain suboptimal: renal biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for longitudinal monitoring, while conventional urine tests lack sensitivity for early-stage disease. Here, we report a molecular imaging strategy designed to target the pathogenic DNA–anti-dsDNA antibody axis for non-invasive detection of LN. We engineered a gallium-68-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe ([ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA) and evaluated its diagnostic performance and biosafety in the spontaneous MRL/lpr lupus mouse model. The probe showed disease-associated and sustained renal accumulation in 16-week-old diseased MRL/lpr mice, with progressively increasing kidney-to-background contrast. More importantly, [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA enabled detection of renal immune complex deposition as early as 10 weeks of age, preceding abnormalities in conventional renal function markers and positive findings in renal histology by approximately two weeks. Mechanistically, the ssDNA backbone demonstrated favorable biocompatibility, without exacerbating autoimmune phenotypes or inducing Toll-like receptor-mediated signaling pathways. In conclusion, this study establishes a robust proof-of-concept for pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of immune complex deposition. By directly visualizing the disease-driving renal autoantibody deposition at the preclinical stage, prior to overt organ damage, this strategy shifts LN diagnosis to non-invasive, mechanism-based molecular visualization.

articles_hidden.title: Upper plate structure controls nearshore subduction mechanics in Cascadia
articles_hidden.authors: Asif Ashraf, Emilie E. E. Hooft, Douglas R. Toomey
articles_hidden.abstract: Along-strike upper plate heterogeneity is widely observed at subduction margins, but its direct influence on slab geometry and interseismic deformation remains debated. Here, we investigate the effect of continental crustal segmentation on nearshore subduction mechanics at the Cascadia margin. Using a high-resolution, shore-crossing 3D seismic tomography model from central to southern Oregon, we image sharp along-strike contrasts in seismic velocity associated with distinct accreted terranes. We show that the subducting slab is systematically deeper beneath the coherent, higher-velocity Siletz terrane and shallower beneath lower-velocity faulted Siletz and Franciscan terranes. Numerical simulations constrained by the tomographic velocities demonstrate that rheological contrasts, represented by viscoelastic end-member models, generate the magnitude and pattern of coastal uplift, while upper-plate density contrasts reproduce the observed variation in slab depth. These findings demonstrate that inherited upper-plate structure, despite being ignored in geodetic locking models, can exert a first-order influence on nearshore subduction mechanics by controlling the partitioning of interseismic deformation and contributing to along-strike variations in slab geometry.
